citation: Knockdown of ZNF233 suppresses hepatocellular carcinoma cell proliferation and tumorigenesis (PMID: 30179682)
summary: ZNF233 (19q13.31; 670-aa Krüppel C2H2-type zinc finger protein) mRNA was markedly up-regulated in HCC tissues compared with matched non-tumorous liver. Its expression correlated with tumor grade, tumor stage and patient prognosis.

citation: Knockdown of ZNF233 suppresses hepatocellular carcinoma cell proliferation and tumorigenesis (PMID: 30179682)
summary: Overexpressing ZNF233 in SMMC-7721 cells promoted G1/S transition and accelerated cell growth. Knockdown in QGY-7701 cells suppressed proliferation in vitro and in xenograft tumors in vivo, where Ki-67-positive cells were reduced. This indicates a positive role in HCC cell growth and suggests ZNF233 as a possible biomarker and therapeutic target.

citation: Integrative transcriptomic and CRISPR dependency analysis identifies hepatoblastoma-specific essential genes and actionable vulnerabilities (PMID: 42385356)
summary: ZNF233 was among the genes overexpressed in hepatoblastoma tumors versus normal liver. In a single-cell deep-learning classifier separating tumor cells from hepatocytes, SHAP analysis identified it as a major contributor, so it is part of an HB-essential/tumor-identity signature. The abstract does not state whether ZNF233 itself was among the 6 genes confirmed absent or lowly expressed in the liver microenvironment.

citation: Adam21 is dispensable for reproductive processes in mice (PMID: 34631320)
phenotype: Normal male fertility; No detectable defects in spermatogenesis; Normal sperm motility and characteristics; No obvious difference in seminiferous epithelium histology compared with wild-type; No detectable defects in meiotic progression; Sertoli cells and Leydig cells appeared normal; No overt reproductive phenotype; Adam21 is not essential for male fertility in mice

citation: Overexpression of a disintegrin and metalloproteinase 21 is associated with motility, metastasis, and poor prognosis in hepatocellular carcinoma (PMID: 29138461)
significance: Multivariate analysis: overall survival P=0.003; recurrence-free survival P=0.001
summary: siRNA knockdown of ADAM21 in KYN-2 HCC cells, which overexpress it, reduced invasion, migration, proliferation, and in vivo metastasis. ADAM21 positivity in patient tumors was associated with vascular invasion, large tumor size, high grade, and poorer overall and recurrence-free survival. It was an independent prognostic risk factor.

citation: The identification of seven metalloproteinase-disintegrin (ADAM) genes from genomic libraries (PMID: 10524237)
summary: ADAM21 was isolated from a human genomic library as an intronless gene with testis-specific expression. One of the pseudogenes isolated in the same screen evolved from ADAM21.

citation: Expression analysis of the Adam21 gene in mouse testis (PMID: 20117247)
summary: Mouse Adam21 produces two transcript types. Germ cell-specific transcripts contain exons 1 and 2, while exon 2-only transcripts are expressed in testicular somatic cells. An essential promoter and repressive regulatory regions were mapped in transfection assays, and protein was confirmed in testicular somatic cells.

citation: Adam21 is dispensable for reproductive processes in mice (PMID: 34631320)
summary: CRISPR/Cas9 Adam21-null male mice had normal fertility, spermatogenesis, sperm motility, and meiotic progression. Sertoli and Leydig cells were also normal, so Adam21 is not essential for male fertility in mice.

citation: A disintegrin and metalloprotease 21 (ADAM21) is associated with neurogenesis and axonal growth in developing and adult rodent CNS (PMID: 16052496)
summary: ADAM21, unlike the other ADAMs tested, is expressed in adult rodent ependyma and SVZ cells with long basal processes. It is also in early postnatal radial glia, in processes extending into the rostral migratory stream, and in growing axonal tracts and olfactory axons. It colocalizes with OMP but not βIII-tubulin, suggesting a role in neuroblast migration, neurogenesis, and late axonal outgrowth or synapse formation.

citation: TCR variable gene involvement in chromosome inversion between 14q11 and 14q24 in adult T-cell leukemia (PMID: 16520872)
summary: A 14q24 gene near the inversion breakpoint, annotated as an ADAM21 pseudogene, was downregulated in an ATL patient. It was found to be expressed and to encode an ADAM21-like protein, and was named ADAM21-L.

citation: Alpha-Dystrobrevin and its associated proteins in human promyelocytic leukemia cells induced to apoptosis (PMID: 22507200)
summary: ADAM21 was identified by immunoprecipitation with anti-α-dystrobrevin followed by mass spectrometry, as a membrane protein associated with α-dystrobrevin in etoposide-treated HL-60 cells.

citation: Functions of 'A disintegrin and metalloproteases (ADAMs)' in the mammalian nervous system (PMID: 31236626)
summary: This review states that ADAM21, a proteolytic ADAM, functions in regenerative processes after neuronal injury, together with ADAM19.

citation: The ADAMs family: coordinators of nervous system development, plasticity and repair (PMID: 16824663)
summary: This review highlights ADAM21 as uniquely associated with neurogenesis and growing axons in the adult brain, making it a potential target for neural repair.

citation: Recurrent targeted genes of hepatitis B virus in the liver cancer genomes identified by a next-generation sequencing-based approach (PMID: 23236287)
summary: ADAM21 was one of the genes targeted by HBV integration in HBV-related HCC. It is listed among genes containing the EGF-like conserved site domain (IPR013032).

citation: Bi-allelic PRMT9 loss-of-function variants cause a syndromic form of intellectual disability (PMID: 41260215)
variant_detail: Single copy gain (duplication) of a region spanning the last exons of PRMT9 and TMEM184C (family Z, individual Z-II.1); exact coordinates not given in the excerpt
phenotype: Individual-level phenotype not given in the excerpt. The cohort is described as having a neurodevelopmental disorder with global developmental delay, learning disabilities, intellectual disability, autism spectrum disorder, epilepsy and hypotonia.
diagnostic_reason: The copy gain was considered relevant to PRMT9 (a possible bi-allelic PRMT9 loss-of-function mechanism), not TMEM184C. No other pathogenic PRMT9 variant in trans was found by Sanger sequencing or WES, and whole-genome sequencing was performed. TMEM184C was only co-involved in the CNV, and no pathogenic role for TMEM184C is claimed.

citation: Biallelic variants in NUDCD2 associated with a multiple malformation syndrome with cholestasis and renal failure (PMID: 37272762)
summary: Two unrelated patients with biallelic NUDCD2 variants had a multiple malformation syndrome: dysmorphic facies, midline brain hypoplasia, hypothyroidism, valve stenosis, liver and kidney failure, hypotonia and early death. Fibroblasts from a patient with biallelic loss-of-function variants lacked NUDCD2 protein. NUDCD2 is described as a Hsp90 co-chaperone that associates with LIS1, HERC2 and cohesin subunits and acts in cell migration and microtubule extension. The syndrome has ciliopathy-like features.

citation: RetSat stabilizes mitotic chromosome segregation in pluripotent stem cells (PMID: 39172275)
summary: In mouse ESCs, RetSat interacts with the cohesin/condensin components Smc1a and Nudcd2, as shown by immunoprecipitation and LC-MS/MS. RetSat deletion reduced the loading of Smc1a, Smc3 and Nudcd2 onto mitotic chromosomes. This links Nudcd2 to chromosome stability and segregation in pluripotent stem cells.

citation: ASHG 2014 - The utility of clinical exome sequencing in identifying the genetic origins of eight unclassified developmental disorders in unique Canadian populations
sample_size: 19 patients by WES across 8 disorders (27 patients in 11 families overall)
summary: Whole exome sequencing identified NUDCD2 as a new disease gene mutated in patients with ataxia, dystonia and mental retardation. NUDCD2 interacts with the lissencephaly-associated protein PAFAH1B1 (LIS1).

citation: Transcriptional response of the bovine endometrium and embryo to endometrial polymorphonuclear neutrophil infiltration as an indicator of subclinical inflammation of the uterine environment (PMID: 22781929)
summary: NUDCD2 was downregulated in blastocysts from cows with subclinical endometritis (SE-7) compared with healthy cows (HE-7). The changes were among genes linked to membrane stability, cell cycle and apoptosis.

citation: Unveiling the unexplored novel signatures for osteoporosis via a detailed bioinformatics and molecular experiments based approach (PMID: 38715824)
summary: NUDCD2 was identified as one of eight hub genes among differentially expressed genes in osteoporosis (GSE35959). RT-qPCR in Pakistani osteoporosis patients confirmed significant downregulation, and ROC analysis showed diagnostic value.

citation: Molecular prognosticators in clinically and pathologically distinct cohorts of head and neck squamous cell carcinoma-A meta-analysis approach (PMID: 31310629)
sample_size: HPV-based meta-analysis, n=83 (8 microarray datasets), validated in TCGA
summary: NUDCD2 was among the genes specifically altered in HPV+ HNSCC. Along with RPP25 and NOVA1, it showed an impact on survival in TCGA validation.

citation: Study on biomarkers of homocysteine-induced transformation of vascular smooth muscle cells into foam cells (PMID: 41644998)
summary: In homocysteine-treated VSMCs, proteomics (LFQ-DIA) found changed NUDCD2 protein levels. PRM validation confirmed the direction of change. NUDCD2 was one of 16 validated proteins, though the follow-up work focused on COX7C.

citation: The role of dinutuximab beta with beta cell function, apoptosis, and proliferation: new approaches to proteomic analysis of insulinoma (PMID: 41123852)
summary: LC-MS/MS proteomics of INS-1 insulinoma cells treated with dinutuximab beta detected NUDCD2 among altered proteins, together with ERP29, ARF1 and others. The protein ubiquitination pathway predominated among the altered pathways.

citation: Peña-Münzenmayer et al. 2015 - Ae4 (Slc4a9) Anion Exchanger Drives Cl- Uptake-dependent Fluid Secretion by Mouse Submandibular Gland Acinar Cells (PMID: 25745107)
phenotype: Saliva secretion reduced by ~35% in Ae4-/- submandibular glands after muscarinic and β-adrenergic stimulation; Reduced HCO3--dependent Cl- uptake in acinar cells, most evident during β-adrenergic/cAMP signaling; Nkcc1 and Na+/H+ exchanger activity not changed; Ae2-/- mice had normal salivation, but reduced HCO3--dependent Cl- uptake; Cl-/HCO3- exchanger activity nearly abolished in double Ae4/Ae2 knockout acinar cells

citation: 2025 - SLC4A9 deficiency is involved in Sjögren's syndrome and enamel defects through RPS27-triggered ribosomal stress (PMID: 42855468)
phenotype: Salivary impairment with reduced saliva secretion; Female-predominant salivary gland inflammation and autoantibody production (Sjögren's-like); Enamel malformation with delayed ameloblast differentiation; Disrupted Cl-/pH homeostasis with RPS27 upregulation and ribosomal stress; p53-dependent cell-cycle arrest and apoptosis in glandular and enamel lineages; Nutlin-3a (MDM2 antagonist) reduced salivary inflammation

citation: Singh et al. 2007 - PAT-1 (Slc26a6) is the predominant apical membrane Cl-/HCO3- exchanger in the upper villous epithelium of the murine duodenum (PMID: 17170027)
phenotype: Basal apical Cl-/HCO3- exchange activity in the upper villous duodenal epithelium reduced by <5% in AE4(-) (Slc4a9-null) mice vs WT, i.e. negligible contribution; SO4(2-)/HCO3- exchange not affected in AE4(-) duodenum

citation: Ae4 (Slc4a9) is an electroneutral monovalent cation-dependent Cl-/HCO3- exchanger (PMID: 27114614)
summary: Native Ae4 in mouse salivary acinar cells and heterologously expressed mouse Ae4 and human AE4 in CHO-K1 cells mediate Na+-dependent Cl-/HCO3- exchange. Na+ moves with HCO3- and the transport is electroneutral. Ae4 also works with K+, Cs+, Li+ and Rb+, so it is a Cl-/nonselective cation-HCO3- exchanger.

citation: Ae4 (Slc4a9) Anion Exchanger Drives Cl- Uptake-dependent Fluid Secretion by Mouse Submandibular Gland Acinar Cells (PMID: 25745107)
summary: Ae4-/- mice had 35% less saliva secretion, with reduced Cl- uptake during β-adrenergic/cAMP stimulation. Nkcc1 and NHE activity were unchanged. Cl-/HCO3- exchange was nearly abolished in Ae2/Ae4 double knockouts, so Ae4 is needed for cAMP-dependent fluid secretion.

citation: Activation of the Ae4 (Slc4a9) cation-driven Cl-/HCO3- exchanger by the cAMP-dependent protein kinase in salivary gland acinar cells (PMID: 34585968)
summary: Ae4 activity in Ae2-/- submandibular acinar cells increased with β-adrenergic stimulation, and H89 (a PKA inhibitor) blocked this. In CHO-K1 cells, co-expressing PKAc increased Ae4 activity. The S173A mutant was not activated by PKA, whereas S273A still was, suggesting Ae4 is regulated through S173 phosphorylation.

citation: The forkhead transcription factor Foxi1 directly activates the AE4 promoter (PMID: 16159312)
summary: AE4 (Slc4a9) is specifically expressed in type B intercalated cells of the renal collecting duct and is absent in Foxi1-null mice. In reporter assays Foxi1 activated the AE4 promoter about 100-fold through one binding site within about 462 bp upstream of the transcription start. Mutating that site abolished both Foxi1 binding and activation, making Slc4a9 a direct Foxi1 target.

citation: Disrupting Hypoxia-Induced Bicarbonate Transport Acidifies Tumor Cells and Suppresses Tumor Growth (PMID: 27197160)
summary: Hypoxia induced SLC4A9 and SLC4A4 expression in cancer cell lines in a manner dependent on HIF1α and HIF2α. SLC4A9 disruption acidified intracellular pH, reduced spheroid growth and increased apoptosis. SLC4A9 RNAi strongly reduced growth of MDA-MB-231 breast tumor and U87 glioma xenografts in mice.

citation: A novel sodium bicarbonate cotransporter-like gene in an ancient duplicated region: SLC4A9 at 5q31 (PMID: 11305939)
summary: SLC4A9 was discovered on chromosome 5q31. It encodes a 990-aa protein with 12 transmembrane domains and a 23-exon gene with 14 mRNA isoforms, produced by extensive alternative splicing. Expression is largely restricted to kidney. It lies in a paralogous EGF-SLC4A-ANK-FGF gene cluster.

citation: SLC4A9 deficiency is involved in Sjögren's syndrome and enamel defects through RPS27-triggered ribosomal stress (PMID: 42855468)
sample_size: 3 amelogenesis imperfecta cases, 1 Sjögren's patient, KO mice
summary: SLC4A9 missense variants were found in three amelogenesis imperfecta cases, and copy number variations with reduced SLC4A9 expression in a Sjögren's syndrome patient. Slc4a9 knockout mice showed reduced salivary secretion, glandular inflammation, and enamel malformation. Loss of SLC4A9 disrupted Cl-/pH homeostasis, upregulated RPS27, caused ribosomal stress and p53-dependent arrest and apoptosis, and Nutlin-3a reduced the inflammation.

citation: Epigenome-Wide Association Study for All-Cause Mortality in a Cardiovascular Cohort Identifies Differential Methylation in CASZ1 (PMID: 31642367)
sample_size: Discovery 55 cases/49 controls; validation 108 cases/108 controls
significance: FDR-adjusted P<0.10 in validation; FDR<0.05 in meta-analysis
summary: In the EWAS validation set, the SLC4A9 CpG cg08215811 was differentially methylated in cases with all-cause mortality (log2 FC = -0.14). It remained significant in the meta-analysis (FDR<0.05). The SLC4A9 transcript failed quality control, so its expression could not be assessed.

citation: Effect of heat stress on the gene expression of ion transporters/channels in the uterus of laying hens during eggshell formation (PMID: 29115887)
summary: SLC4A9 is expressed in the uterine lining of laying hens during eggshell formation. Heat stress reduced SLC4A9 transcript by 66.1%, along with ITPR3 and SLC4A4, which may impair Cl-/HCO3-/Na+ transport during eggshell mineralization.

citation: Integrated compensatory network is activated in the absence of NCC phosphorylation (PMID: 25893600)
summary: In SPAK kinase-deficient mice, which cannot activate NCC, Slc4a9 was coordinately induced along with Slc26a4 and Slc4a8, carbonic anhydrases and V-ATPase subunits in pendrin-positive intercalated cells. This forms a compensatory NaCl reabsorption transport system.

citation: Kuo et al. 2005 - Dosage-dependent requirement for mouse Vezf1 in vascular system development (PMID: 15882861)
phenotype: Homozygous mutants: vascular remodeling defects; Homozygous mutants: loss of vascular integrity with localized hemorrhaging; Homozygous mutants: defective endothelial cell adhesion and tight junction formation in vessels; Heterozygous mutants: haploinsufficiency with lymphatic hypervascularization; Heterozygous mutants: hemorrhaging and edema in the jugular region, reminiscent of cystic hygroma
knockout_type: full knockout (homozygous) and heterozygous knockout (targeted inactivation)

citation: Vezf1 regulates cardiac structure and contractile function (PMID: 31911272)
phenotype: Reduced cardiac growth; Impaired ventricular contractile response to β-adrenergic stimuli; No dysregulation of cardiomyocyte Ca2+ transient kinetics; Dysregulation of cardiac muscle contraction and dilated cardiomyopathy related genes; Myh7/β-MHC identified as a key target

citation: ETV2 and VEZF1 interaction and regulation of the hematoendothelial lineage during embryogenesis (PMID: 36923254)
phenotype: Downregulation of hematoendothelial marker genes during embryoid body mesodermal differentiation
organism: mouse (Vezf1 knockout embryonic stem cells, in vitro embryoid body differentiation)

citation: The transcription factor Vezf1 represses the expression of the antiangiogenic factor Cited2 in endothelial cells (PMID: 29794136)
phenotype: Increased Cited2 expression; Inefficient differentiation into endothelial cells; Defective tube formation; Reduced activation of EC-specific genes with lower H3K27 acetylation at their promoters; Cited2 shRNA depletion reduced the angiogenic defects
organism: mouse (Vezf1-/- embryonic stem cells, in vitro)

citation: Zhao et al. 2023 - VEZF1 loss-of-function mutation underlying familial dilated cardiomyopathy (PMID: 36657711)
summary: Whole-exome sequencing of a DCM family identified a heterozygous VEZF1 nonsense mutation, p.(Lys164*), that segregated with autosomal dominant DCM with complete penetrance. The mutation was absent from 200 unrelated DCM patients, 400 controls and population databases. In dual-luciferase assays the mutant failed to transactivate the MYH7 and ET1 promoters, indicating loss of function.

citation: Vezf1 regulates cardiac structure and contractile function (PMID: 31911272)
summary: Vezf1 expression is decreased in diseased human myocardium and mouse hearts. Zebrafish Vezf1 knockdown reduced cardiac growth and impaired the ventricular contractile response to β-adrenergic stimulation. Myh7/β-MHC is a key target, acting through an MCAT site in its promoter, and TEAD-1 is a Vezf1 binding partner.

citation: ETV2 and VEZF1 interaction and regulation of the hematoendothelial lineage during embryogenesis (PMID: 36923254)
summary: A yeast two-hybrid screen identified VEZF1 as an ETV2 binding partner, confirmed by co-IP and GST pull-down. VEZF1 is expressed specifically in endothelium and binds the Flt1 promoter, where it co-activates transcription with ETV2. Vezf1 knockout ESCs showed reduced hematoendothelial marker expression, while VEZF1 overexpression induced these genes.

citation: VEZF1-guanine quadruplex DNA interaction regulates alternative polyadenylation and detyrosinase activity of VASH1 (PMID: 33231681)
summary: VEZF1 binds DNA G-quadruplex structures in vitro and in cells, which sets the ratio of the VASH1 long and short mRNA isoforms. Loss of VEZF1 or G4 stabilization increased the long VASH1 isoform and tubulin detyrosinase activity, and diminished angiogenesis in HUVECs.

citation: Vezf1 regulates genomic DNA methylation through its effects on expression of DNA methyltransferase Dnmt3b (PMID: 18676812)
summary: Vezf1-/- mouse ESCs lose DNA methylation at widespread sites, including Line1 elements, minor satellites, imprinted genes and CpG islands. The loss is attributed to a substantial decrease in Dnmt3b abundance.

citation: Vezf1 protein binding sites genome-wide are associated with pausing of elongating RNA polymerase II (PMID: 22308494)
summary: In HeLaS3 cells, Vezf1 binding correlates genome-wide with peaks of elongating Ser2-P Pol II, reflecting Vezf1-dependent slowing of elongation. Loss of Vezf1 in mES cells reduces Pol II accumulation at its sites and alters alternative splicing. Vezf1 interacts with Mrg15/Mrgbp, a reader of H3K36me3.

citation: The transcription factor Vezf1 represses the expression of the antiangiogenic factor Cited2 in endothelial cells (PMID: 29794136)
summary: Vezf1-/- mouse ESCs had increased Cited2 expression and differentiated inefficiently into endothelial cells, with tube-formation defects and reduced H3K27ac at EC gene promoters. Cited2 shRNA knockdown rescued the angiogenic defects. The results support Vezf1 acting as an insulator-like repressor of Cited2.

citation: RhoB controls coordination of adult angiogenesis and lymphangiogenesis following injury by regulating VEZF1-mediated transcription (PMID: 24280686)
summary: Nuclear RhoB-GTP controls distinct gene sets in blood versus lymphatic endothelial cells by regulating VEZF1-mediated transcription. A small-molecule inhibitor of the VEZF1-DNA interaction recapitulated RhoB loss in ischaemic retinopathy.

citation: Vezf1/DB1 is an endothelial cell-specific transcription factor that regulates expression of the endothelin-1 promoter (PMID: 11504723)
summary: Vezf1/DB1 is a nuclear, endothelial-specific zinc finger protein that activates the human endothelin-1 promoter. It acts through an ACCCCC element 47 bp upstream of the transcription start site, and a 2-bp mutation in this element abolished responsiveness.

citation: GFAT1 promotes the progression of hepatocellular carcinoma via enhancing the O-GlcNAcylation of VEZF1 (PMID: 40858565)
summary: VEZF1 is heavily O-GlcNAcylated in GFAT1-overexpressing hepatoma cells. Modification at Ser123 and Ser124 reduces its proteasomal degradation and promotes TNS1 transcription. A VEZF1-derived competing peptide reduced TNS1 expression and suppressed HCC progression in mice.

citation: Iossifov et al. 2012 - De novo gene disruptions in children on the autistic spectrum (PMID: 22542183)
variant_detail: Family 13092, male proband: de novo insertion ins(AGGTCAG) in LMTK3 (affected residue ~307/1,490); the exact HGVS notation is not given. The row assignment is inferred from a garbled table.
phenotype: Autism spectrum disorder
diagnostic_reason: De novo gene-disrupting (frameshift indel) variant found by exome sequencing in a child with autism. The study's cohort-level excess of de novo gene-disrupting mutations in affected children over unaffected siblings supports its relevance. No gene-specific functional or segregation evidence is given.
center_country: Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory, USA (Simons Simplex Collection families)

citation: Lmtk3-KO Mice Display a Range of Behavioral Abnormalities and Have an Impairment in GluA1 Trafficking (PMID: 31310731)
phenotype: hyper-sociability; prepulse inhibition (PPI) deficits; cognitive dysfunction; behavioral abnormalities linked to psychiatric disease, suppressed by clozapine treatment; severely impaired LTP induction; abnormal GluA1 trafficking after AMPA stimulation in KO neurons; reduced GluA1 expression in the post-synaptic density

citation: LMTK3 deficiency causes pronounced locomotor hyperactivity and impairs endocytic trafficking (PMID: 24760852)
phenotype: pronounced locomotor hyperactivity; reduced anxiety behavior; decreased depression-like behavior; increased striatal dopamine metabolite levels and dopamine turnover rate; impaired endocytic trafficking of NMDA receptors in cultured primary neurons; no histological abnormalities in the brain (per citing review)

citation: The structure-function relationship of oncogenic LMTK3 (PMID: 33188023)
summary: The 2.1Å crystal structure of the LMTK3 kinase domain was solved, and its consensus motif, phosphoproteome and substrates were defined. LMTK3 is an HSP90 client that needs HSP90 for folding and stability. The inhibitor C28 triggers proteasomal degradation of LMTK3, increases apoptosis in breast cancer cells, reduces proliferation across the NCI-60 panel, and slows xenograft and transgenic breast tumor growth.

citation: LMTK3 regulation of EV biogenesis and cargo sorting promotes tumour growth by reducing monocyte infiltration and driving pro-tumourigenic macrophage polarisation in breast cancer (PMID: 40405280)
summary: LMTK3 phosphorylates Rab7, which reduces MVB-lysosome fusion and alters EV size, subpopulations and cargo. LMTK3 increases PSAT1 packaging in EVs, which upregulates PHGDH in monocytes, reduces monocyte infiltration and promotes M2-like macrophage polarisation. LMTK3 inhibition reverses these effects.

citation: LMTK3 Represses Tumor Suppressor-like Genes through Chromatin Remodeling in Breast Cancer (PMID: 26212333)
summary: LMTK3 ChIP-seq binding correlates with repressive chromatin marks. LMTK3 binds KAP1, and the interaction is stabilized by PP1α, which blocks KAP1 phosphorylation at LMTK3-bound chromatin. This condenses chromatin, tethers it to the nuclear periphery with H3K9me3, and silences tumor suppressor-like genes.

citation: LMTK3 escapes tumour suppressor miRNAs via sequestration of DDX5 (PMID: 26739063)
summary: LMTK3 interacts with DDX5 (p68) and binds, via DDX5, the pri-miRNAs of miR-34a, miR-196a2 and miR-182, sequestering them from Microprocessor processing. miR-34a and miR-182 in turn bind the LMTK3 3'UTR and inhibit its stability and translation, forming a feedback loop.

citation: LMTK3 promotes tumorigenesis in bladder cancer via the ERK/MAPK pathway (PMID: 32865871)
summary: LMTK3 is overexpressed in bladder cancer, and high expression predicts poor overall survival. Knockdown causes G2/M arrest, apoptosis and reduced EMT-linked migration, and lowers MEK/ERK1/2 phosphorylation. Overexpression promotes proliferation and migration, which the MEK inhibitor U0126 rescues.

citation: LMTK3 is essential for oncogenic KIT expression in KIT-mutant GIST and melanoma (PMID: 30242244)
summary: A tyrosine kinome siRNA screen identified LMTK3 as a regulator of KIT translation rate. LMTK3 silencing reduced total KIT and downstream signaling, decreased viability and increased death in KIT-dependent GIST and melanoma lines, including those with TKI-resistant secondary KIT mutations. LMTK3 siRNA also delayed GIST xenograft growth.

citation: Lmtk3-KO Mice Display a Range of Behavioral Abnormalities and Have an Impairment in GluA1 Trafficking (PMID: 31310731)
summary: Lmtk3-knockout mice show hyper-sociability, PPI deficits and cognitive dysfunction, which clozapine suppressed. They also have severely impaired LTP, abnormal GluA1 trafficking after AMPA stimulation, and reduced GluA1 in the postsynaptic density.

citation: The lncRNA MIR2052HG regulates ERα levels and aromatase inhibitor resistance through LMTK3 by recruiting EGR1 (PMID: 30944027)
summary: MIR2052HG recruits EGR1 to the LMTK3 promoter to drive LMTK3 transcription, in a SNP- and aromatase inhibitor-dependent manner. LMTK3 sustains ERα levels by reducing PKC activity, which raises AKT/FOXO3-driven ESR1 transcription and limits PKC/MEK/ERK/RSK1-mediated ERα degradation.

citation: LMTK3 confers chemo-resistance in breast cancer (PMID: 29540829)
sample_size: four clinical cohorts of pre-/post-chemotherapy breast tumor pairs
summary: LMTK3 overexpression reduced doxorubicin sensitivity in 2D and 3D cultures and in mice. It delayed γH2AX-marked double-strand breaks and lowered ATM phosphorylation. Doxorubicin differentially regulated more than 700 genes depending on LMTK3 level, and LMTK3 IHC rose after chemotherapy in four clinical cohorts.

citation: LMTK3 knockdown retards cell growth and invasion and promotes apoptosis in thyroid cancer (PMID: 28260052)
sample_size: 102 thyroid carcinoma, 52 benign tumor, 50 healthy volunteers
summary: Serum LMTK3 was higher in thyroid carcinoma than in benign tumors and healthy controls. LMTK3 protein and mRNA were higher in cancer tissue and associated with disease stage. Knockdown in SW579 cells reduced proliferation, invasion and migration and induced apoptosis.

citation: The 12q14 microdeletion syndrome: six new cases confirming the role of HMGA2 in growth (PMID: 21267005)
variant_detail: 12q14 interstitial microdeletions (within a 12q13.3q15 range) encompassing LEMD3 and HMGA2; exact breakpoints not given in the abstract
phenotype: significant short stature; no osteopoikilosis despite LEMD3 deletion; developmental delay; significant speech delay; subtle facial dysmorphism; congenital heart defects (in the overall 6-patient series)
diagnostic_reason: Array-detected 12q14 deletions, 4 of 6 confirmed de novo in the series. Short stature was attributed to HMGA2 deletion. LEMD3 deletion did not produce osteopoikilosis in the two patients whose deletions included it.
center_country: Three diagnostic testing centres (country not stated in abstract)

citation: LEMD3 organizes the 3D chromatin architecture to maintain vascular smooth muscle cell identity (PMID: 41044070)
phenotype: Lemd3 deficiency in VSMCs causes loss of the contractile phenotype; exacerbated intimal hyperplasia; disturbed chromatin structure with increased inter-TAD interactions at A/B compartment boundaries; decreased chromatin accessibility; repressed expression of VSMC contractile genes

citation: Perturbations of BMP/TGF-β and VEGF/VEGFR signalling pathways in non-syndromic sporadic brain arteriovenous malformations (BAVM) (PMID: 30120215)
phenotype: A transgenic zebrafish model was used to functionally validate the pathogenic variants, including a damaging LEMD3 variant found in a BAVM patient; The abstract does not give the specific zebrafish phenotypes or whether knockdown or variant overexpression was used

citation: Hellemans et al. 2004 - Loss-of-function mutations in LEMD3 result in osteopoikilosis, Buschke-Ollendorff syndrome and melorheostosis (PMID: 15489854)
phenotype: XMAN1, the Xenopus laevis ortholog of LEMD3, antagonizes BMP signaling during embryogenesis; This is prior work cited in the abstract; the Xenopus experiments were not performed in this study, and the study itself reports human LEMD3 loss-of-function mutations

citation: 2025 - The inner nuclear membrane protein LEMD3 organizes the 3D chromatin architecture to maintain vascular smooth muscle cell identity (PMID: 41044070)
summary: A genome-scale CRISPR screen identified LEMD3 as a regulator of VSMC identity. Lemd3 deficiency caused loss of the contractile phenotype and worsened intimal hyperplasia in mice. Lemd3 depletion increased inter-TAD interactions at A/B compartment boundaries, reduced chromatin accessibility and repressed contractile gene expression.

citation: 2025 - The inner nuclear membrane protein LEMD3 organizes the 3D chromatin architecture to maintain vascular smooth muscle cell identity (PMID: 41044070) [protein interactome]
summary: Protein interactome analysis showed LEMD3 interacts with CBX3 (HP1γ), a reader of H3K9me2/3. This interaction anchors heterochromatin at the nuclear periphery.

citation: Hsa_circ_0070963 inhibits liver fibrosis via regulation of miR-223-3p and LEMD3 (PMID: 32003753)
summary: LEMD3 is a validated target of miR-223-3p (luciferase reporter and rescue experiments) and is responsible for hepatic stellate cell activation. The hsa_circ_0070963/miR-223-3p/LEMD3 axis regulates HSC activation in vitro and in vivo. Hsa_circ_0070963 acts as a miR-223-3p sponge, and its levels fall during liver fibrosis.

citation: Identification of unique venous thromboembolism-susceptibility variants in African-Americans (PMID: 28203683)
summary: In a GWAS of VTE in African-Americans, the intragenic LEMD3 SNP rs138916004 reached genome-wide significance. The SNP is present only in Africans. LEMD3 was also differentially expressed in GEO and Mayo Clinic expression datasets. LEMD3 encodes an antagonist of TGF-β-induced proliferation arrest.

citation: LEM-domain proteins are lost during human spermiogenesis but BAF and BAF-L persist (PMID: 28684548)
summary: RT-PCR, immunofluorescence and western blotting showed LEMD3 is absent in human spermatids, as are Emerin and LBR. LEMD1, LEMD2 short isoform, ANKLE2, LAP2β, BAF and BAF-L are present. The lamina-chromatin interface in spermatids therefore differs from that in somatic cells.

citation: The heterozygous Lemd3 +/GT mouse is not a murine model for osteopoikilosis in humans (PMID: 19862465)
summary: Heterozygous Lemd3 gene-trap mice showed no osteopoikilosis-like lesions on X-ray, microCT or histology, and no significant differences in bone histomorphometric parameters. LEMD3 is described as an inner nuclear membrane protein that antagonizes BMP/TGFβ signaling via R-SMADs. Haploinsufficiency in mouse does not reproduce the human bone phenotype.

citation: Deactivating germline mutations in LEMD3 cause osteopoikilosis and Buschke-Ollendorff syndrome, but not sporadic melorheostosis (PMID: 17087626)
summary: Heterozygous loss-of-function LEMD3 mutations (p.L478X, p.Y441X, frameshift c.332_333insTC, p.R655X) were found in familial OPK and BOS, including a case with melorheostosis-like lesions. No mutations were found in sporadic melorheostosis.

citation: Germline LEMD3 mutations are rare in sporadic patients with isolated melorheostosis (PMID: 16470551)
sample_size: 5 OPK/BOS probands, 2 BOS-melorheostosis families, 12 isolated melorheostosis patients
summary: Seven novel LEMD3 loss-of-function mutations were identified in OPK/BOS patients, including families with BOS and melorheostosis. No germline or somatic mosaic LEMD3 mutations were found in most sporadic isolated melorheostosis.

citation: Identification of a novel LEMD3 Y871X mutation in a three-generation family with osteopoikilosis and review of the literature (PMID: 26694706)
summary: A novel heterozygous frameshift c.2612_2613insA (p.Y871X) in exon 13 of LEMD3 co-segregated with osteopoikilosis across three generations and was absent in controls. It is predicted to cause a premature stop codon.

citation: ASHG 2011 - A novel mutation in the gene LEMD3 in a patient with sub-clinical Osteopoikilosis
summary: A heterozygous missense variant (R901W, c.2701C>T) in the C-terminal nucleoplasmic region of LEMD3 segregated with sub-clinical osteopoikilosis in an Azorean family. This region (aa 789-911) is predicted to be a U2AF homology motif (RRM-like) protein-interaction domain.

citation: Comparative analysis of the autism‑related variants between different autistic children in a family pedigree (PMID: 34368859)
phenotype: autism spectrum disorder
diagnostic_reason: Rare heterozygous missense variant shared by both autistic siblings (IV2 and IV4) in a family pedigree on WES, passing the harmfulness and quality filters. However, ATP2B4 was not among the credible autism-related genes (AutismKB score >16) highlighted by the authors, so pathogenicity is not established.

citation: Aravindan et al. 2021 - The plasma membrane calcium ATPase 4 does not influence parasite levels but partially promotes experimental cerebral malaria during murine blood stage malaria (PMID: 34215257)
phenotype: Reduced red blood cell size and haemoglobin content; Normal RBC maturation and reticulocyte count; No change in peripheral parasite burden or dynamics with P. chabaudi, P. yoelii or P. berghei infection; Slight protection against experimental cerebral malaria (P. berghei); Minor reduction in antigen-experienced T cell accumulation in the brain

citation: Pmca4 KO B-cell study 2020 - Plasma membrane Ca(2+) ATPase 1 (PMCA1) but not PMCA4 is critical for B-cell development and Ca(2+) homeostasis in mice (PMID: 33098669)
phenotype: Normal B-cell development in Pmca4 (Atp2b4) KO mice; Normal calcium handling in Pmca4-/- B cells; Mouse and human naive B cells express PMCA1 but not PMCA4 (T cells do express PMCA4)

citation: Okunade et al. 2004 - Targeted ablation of plasma membrane Ca2+-ATPase (PMCA) 1 and 4 indicates a major housekeeping function for PMCA1 and a critical role in hyperactivated sperm motility and male fertility for PMCA4 (PMID: 15178683)
phenotype: No embryonic lethality; Pmca4-/- mice outwardly normal; Male infertility with normal spermatogenesis and mating behavior; Sperm failed to achieve hyperactivated motility, with normal motility before capacitation; Increased mitochondrial condensation in sperm tails, indicating Ca2+ overload; Normal ultrastructure of the sperm tail motility apparatus; Impaired phasic contractions and apoptosis in portal vein smooth muscle in vitro, strain-dependent (absent on Black Swiss background unless also Pmca1+/-); Pmca1 null mice were embryonic lethal, Pmca1 heterozygotes had no overt phenotype

citation: Lessard et al. 2017 - An erythroid-specific ATP2B4 enhancer mediates red blood cell hydration and malaria susceptibility (PMID: 28714864)
summary: Erythroblast eQTL mapping found erythroid-specific eQTLs for ATP2B4 at the same SNPs associated with MCHC and severe malaria. Atp2b4-/- mice have increased MCHC. CRISPR deletion of the erythroid enhancer raised intracellular calcium in erythroid cells, supporting ATP2B4 as the causal gene at this locus.

citation: ASHG 2016 - Combining eQTL analyses with CRISPR/Cas9 experiments to fine-map causal variants that regulate ATP2B4, a gene associated with red blood cell traits and malaria resistance
sample_size: 534 genes with allelic imbalance; 215 with eQTL in erythroblasts
summary: A cluster of SNPs in an erythroid-specific DHS is an eQTL for ATP2B4. CRISPR deletion of the DHS in a human erythroid cell line reduced ATP2B4 expression in a dose-dependent way, and bi-allelic deletion nearly abolished it. The essential element was narrowed to a 98 bp region with 5 GATA1 motifs that appear to act cooperatively.

citation: Identification of ATP2B4 Regulatory Element Containing Functional Genetic Variants Associated with Severe Malaria (PMID: 35563239)
significance: Significant association with severe malaria (Senegalese population)
summary: Five ATP2B4 SNPs in LD with rs10900585 lie in a regulatory region associated with severe malaria in a Senegalese cohort. Individual SNPs and their combination had regulatory effects. CRISPR/Cas9 deletion of the region in K562 cells decreased ATP2B4 transcript and protein and raised intracellular Ca2+.

citation: Genetic variations in human ATP2B4 gene alter Plasmodium falciparum in vitro growth in RBCs from Gambian adults (PMID: 36604655)
significance: p<0.0001 for PMCA4b expression and calcium t½; p<0.01 for parasite growth
summary: Recall-by-genotype study of rs1541252. C/C homozygote RBCs had reduced PMCA4b protein and slower calcium expulsion. P. falciparum growth was lower in these RBCs, while adhesion and var-gene expression were unchanged. The PMCA4b inhibitor aurintricarboxylic acid also inhibited parasite growth.

citation: Decreased calcium pump expression in human erythrocytes is connected to a minor haplotype in the ATP2B4 gene (PMID: 28216081)
summary: Some healthy volunteers had markedly reduced RBC PMCA4b by flow cytometry and western blot, with no compensation by other PMCA isoforms and lower calcium extrusion. Low PMCA4b correlated with a minor haplotype in the predicted second promoter region, the same haplotype linked to MCHC and malaria protection in GWAS.

citation: ATP2B4 is an essential gene for epidermal growth factor-induced macropinocytosis in A431 cells (PMID: 38597132)
summary: ATP2B4 (PMCA4) knockout in A431 cells blocked ruffle closure and macropinosome formation but not ruffle formation, and reduced EGF-stimulated Ca2+ oscillations. Pump activity itself was required, independent of its C-terminal PDZ-binding motif.

citation: Molecular and Electrophysiological Analyses of ATP2B4 Gene Variants in Bilateral Adrenal Hyperaldosteronism (PMID: 32002807)
summary: Rare ATP2B4 variants from BHA patients did not alter basal or agonist-stimulated CYP11B2 expression in HAC15 adrenal cells, unlike the ATP2B3 control. ATP2B4 is expressed in adrenal tissue, and HAC15 cells show endogenous ATP2B4 conductance. Knockdown reduced angiotensin II response in only 1 of 4 shRNA clones, so no pathogenic role in BHA was confirmed.

citation: Ultrastructural and immunohistochemical localization of plasma membrane Ca2+-ATPase 4 in Ca2+-transporting epithelia (PMID: 26180241)
summary: Pmca4 was found only in intestinal smooth muscle, not enterocytes. In kidney it was broadly expressed in the distal nephron (highest in TRPV5- and NCC-positive segments), at the basolateral membrane and perinuclear compartments. Expression was unchanged by Ca2+ balance perturbations, suggesting a housekeeping role.

citation: Molecular signatures of labor and nonlabor myometrium with parsimonious classification from 2 calcium transporter genes (PMID: 33945511)
summary: The ATP2B4/ATP2A2 expression ratio separated nonquiescent from quiescent human myometrium in RNA-seq, two public datasets, and qPCR. This links ATP2B4 (PMCA4) expression to the myometrial contractile program.

citation: Circadian miR-449c-5p regulates uterine Ca(2+) transport during eggshell calcification in chickens (PMID: 34702171)
summary: ATP2B4 mRNA and protein are rhythmically expressed in chicken uterus and are a direct target of miR-449c-5p, confirmed by dual-luciferase assay. ATP2B4 overexpression lowered intracellular Ca2+ and knockdown raised it, supporting a role in uterine trans-epithelial Ca2+ transport.

citation: Chen et al. 2024 - RAB17 promotes endometrial cancer progression by inhibiting TFRC-dependent ferroptosis (PMID: 39242574)
summary: RAB17 is more highly expressed in endometrial cancer tissue than in peritumoral tissue. It suppresses ferroptosis by reducing TFRC protein via ubiquitin-proteasome-dependent degradation. Low glucose raises RAB17 expression, and the RAB17-TFRC axis supports EC cell survival under glucose deprivation. Findings were corroborated in vivo and in clinical data.

citation: Single-cell RNA-seq and bulk-seq identify RAB17 as a potential regulator of angiogenesis by human dermal microvascular endothelial cells in diabetic foot ulcers (PMID: 37605780)
summary: RAB17 was identified by scRNA-seq, bulk-seq, WGCNA and LASSO as a marker whose expression is significantly reduced in DFU-derived HDMECs. Overexpressing RAB17 enhanced angiogenesis, HIF-1α and VEGFA expression, and diabetic wound healing, partly via MAPK/ERK signalling.

citation: Down-regulation of Rab17 promotes tumourigenic properties of hepatocellular carcinoma cells via Erk pathway (PMID: 26191189)
summary: Rab17 was present in 75% of paraneoplastic tissues but only 35% of HCC samples. Knockdown in Hep3B and Huh-7 cells increased proliferation, invasion, migration, xenograft growth and angiogenesis. These effects were reversed by an Erk pathway inhibitor, suggesting Rab17 acts as a tumor suppressor.

citation: ALS2, the small GTPase Rab17-interacting protein, regulates maturation and sorting of Rab17-associated endosomes (PMID: 31959474)
summary: Rab17 localizes to recycling endosomes in a Rab11-dependent manner and interacts with ALS2 and RABGEF1. RABGEF1 acts as a Rab17 GEF, whereas ALS2 only binds Rab17 and acts downstream of RABGEF1 to mature Rab17-positive nascent endosomes into EEA1-positive early endosomes. These endosomes arise via clathrin-independent endocytosis.

citation: Rab17 regulates apical delivery of hepatic transcytotic vesicles (PMID: 30256711)
summary: Rab17 is monosumoylated (K68), which likely mediates interaction with apical syntaxin 2. In polarized WIF-B hepatic cells, Rab17 regulates basolateral-to-apical transcytotic vesicle docking and fusion. GTP-bound and sumoylated Rab17 are needed for apical docking, and GTP hydrolysis is needed for vesicle delivery.

citation: Downregulation of Rab17 promotes cell proliferation and invasion in non-small cell lung cancer through STAT3/HIF-1α/VEGF signaling (PMID: 31841274)
summary: Low Rab17 expression correlates with poor overall survival in NSCLC. Knockdown promotes proliferation, invasion, angiogenesis, xenograft growth, EMT (decreased E-cadherin, increased Vimentin and β-catenin) and reduced apoptosis, partly through STAT3/HIF-1α/VEGF signaling.

citation: A proteomic approach to identify endosomal cargoes controlling cancer invasiveness (PMID: 28062852)
summary: Rab17 is suppressed by ERK2 signalling. Rab17 knockdown selectively reduces the v-SNARE Vamp8, which associates with Rab17 at late endosomes. Loss of Rab17 or Vamp8 increases mobilisation of NRP2-containing late endosomes and NRP2 surface expression, promoting DCIS invasiveness.

citation: LMO4 promotes OSCC progression by inducing RAB17 degradation and ferroptosis resistance (PMID: 41213908)
summary: LMO4 promotes ubiquitin-proteasome-dependent degradation of RAB17, a tumor suppressor in OSCC, thereby increasing ferroptosis resistance, proliferation and migration. Restoring RAB17 reduced these behaviors, and high-LMO4 xenografts had lower RAB17 protein.

citation: The recycling endosome protein Rab17 regulates melanocytic filopodia formation and melanosome trafficking (PMID: 21291502)
summary: GFP-Rab17 localizes to recycling endosomes and melanosomes, and Rab17 mRNA is regulated by MITF. Rab17 knockdown causes melanosome accumulation at the periphery, intracellular melanin accumulation and reduced filopodia formation. Rab17 acts downstream of Rab27a.

citation: Rab17 localizes to recycling endosomes and regulates receptor-mediated transcytosis in epithelial cells (PMID: 9624171)
summary: Rab17 is restricted to epithelial cells and its expression is induced during polarization. In MDCK cells it localizes to apical recycling endosomes, and its overexpression impairs basolateral-to-apical transcytosis of dimeric IgA via pIgR.

citation: Pf1/Phf12 knockout study 2016 - The Chromatin-Associated Phf12 Protein Maintains Nucleolar Integrity and Prevents Premature Cellular Senescence (PMID: 27956701)
phenotype: Required for mid- to late gestation viability; Pf1-deficient MEFs have impaired proliferative potential; Decreased BrdU incorporation in MEFs; Increased senescence-associated β-galactosidase activity (premature cellular senescence); Elevated phosphorylated H2AX (γ-H2A.X), indicating DNA double-strand breaks; Dysregulated ribosome biogenesis pathway transcripts; Abnormal nucleolar structure in Pf1-deficient cells; Pf1-interacting proteins enriched for ribosome biogenesis factors

citation: Mouse knockout study - The Chromatin-Associated Phf12 Protein Maintains Nucleolar Integrity and Prevents Premature Cellular Senescence (PMID: 27956701)
summary: Pf1/Phf12 knockout mice die in mid-to-late gestation. Pf1-deficient MEFs show reduced proliferation and BrdU incorporation, increased SA-β-Gal and γ-H2AX, abnormal nucleolar structure and dysregulated ribosome biogenesis transcripts. Pf1 is therefore required for nucleolar integrity and prevents premature senescence.

citation: Proteomic analysis in Phf12 study - The Chromatin-Associated Phf12 Protein Maintains Nucleolar Integrity and Prevents Premature Cellular Senescence (PMID: 27956701)
summary: Pf1 associates with a chromatin complex containing MRG15, Sin3B and HDAC1 that acts as a transcriptional modulator. Proteomic analysis of Pf1-interacting complexes identified proteins involved in ribosome biogenesis.

citation: Epigenetic inactivation of miR-203 as a key step in neural crest epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (PMID: 30910825)
summary: Phf12 is a key regulator of neural crest delamination, together with Snail2. It shows a reciprocal expression pattern with miR-203 during the neural crest EMT, and miR-203 interacts with its 3'UTR. Ectopic miR-203 inhibits neural crest migration in chick, and miR-203 inhibition causes premature delamination.

citation: MYC promotes cancer progression by modulating m(6)A modifications to suppress target gene translation (PMID: 33426808)
summary: PHF12 is a MYC-repressed gene. MYC activates ALKBH5, which lowers m6A in PHF12 mRNA, and YTHDF3 reads this mark to control PHF12 translation. Overexpressing PHF12 (or SPI1) suppresses growth of MYC-driven B-cell lymphomas in vitro and in vivo, so PHF12 acts as a growth suppressor in this context.

citation: PHF12 regulates HDAC1 to promote tumorigenesis via EGFR/AKT signaling pathway in non-small cell lung cancer (PMID: 39075515)
summary: PHF12 is upregulated in NSCLC tumor tissue and correlates with HDAC1. ChIP showed PHF12 transcriptionally regulates HDAC1. PHF12 knockdown reduced proliferation, migration and xenograft growth, and HDAC1 overexpression rescued these effects. The PHF12-HDAC1 axis activates EGFR/AKT signaling.

citation: Invasive phenotype in triple negative breast cancer is inhibited by blocking SIN3A-PF1 interaction through KLF9 mediated repression of ITGA6 and ITGB1 (PMID: 34968869)
summary: PF1 (PHF12) binds the SIN3A PAH2 domain through its SID and forms a complex with MRG15 and KDM5A/B. Disrupting PF1/SIN3A with PF1-SID in TNBC cells reduced invasion, migration and mammosphere formation and induced senescence. It also increased SIN3A and KLF9 occupancy at the ITGA6 and ITGB1 promoters and repressed those genes.

citation: LncRNA RP11-116G8.5 promotes the progression of lung squamous cell carcinoma through sponging miR-3150b-3p/miR-6870-5p to upregulate PHF12/FOXP4 (PMID: 34500373)
summary: PHF12 is a direct target of miR-3150b-3p, shown by luciferase reporter and Ago2-RIP assays, and is upregulated by the RP11-116G8.5 sponge. PHF12 overexpression reversed the anti-proliferative, anti-migratory and anti-invasive effects of RP11-116G8.5 knockdown in LUSC cells, so it acts as an oncogenic effector.

citation: Family-based exome sequencing identifies rare coding variants in age-related macular degeneration (PMID: 32246154)
summary: Rare protein-altering PHF12 variants were found in three or more multiplex AMD families. PHF12 lies at an AMD-GWAS locus and is proposed as a candidate causal gene.

citation: Identifying drug candidates for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma based on integrative multiomics analysis (PMID: 38989421)
summary: PHF12 was one of four hub genes in a methylation-based PDAC diagnostic model. Its protein level was upregulated in PDAC tumor tissue compared with adjacent normal tissue.

citation: Using gene expression from urine sediment to diagnose prostate cancer: development of a new multiplex mRNA urine test and validation of current biomarkers (PMID: 26856686)
summary: PHF12 transcript level in post-prostatic massage urine sediment was an independent predictor discriminating prostate cancer patients from controls, among 42 genes tested by qPCR.

citation: Unknown et al. 2025 - HNF4α-Mediated LINC02560 Promotes Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma Progression by Targeting the miR-505-5p/PDE4C Axis (PMID: 40427523)
summary: In PTC cell lines (KTC-1, BCPAP), LINC02560 sponges miR-505-5p and relieves its suppression of PDE4C. This activates P-AKT and EMT signaling and promotes proliferation, migration and invasion. HNF4α drives LINC02560 expression, so the HNF4α/LINC02560/miR-505-5p/PDE4C axis acts oncogenically in PTC.

citation: Integrated analysis using methylation and gene expression microarrays reveals PDE4C as a prognostic biomarker in human glioma (PMID: 24842301)
sample_size: 124 patient samples (56 low-grade, 63 high-grade glioma, 5 normal brain)
summary: PDE4C promoter is hypermethylated and its expression reduced in high-grade glioma, which correlates with grade progression and poorer survival. Demethylation with 5-Aza-dC upregulated PDE4C in glioma cell lines. PDE4C siRNA reduced WT p53, and in U87 cells PDE4C promoted apoptosis and inhibited migration, suggesting a tumor-suppressor role via the p53 pathway.

citation: Multiple splice variants of phosphodiesterase PDE4C cloned from human lung and testis (PMID: 9349724)
summary: Cloned multiple human PDE4C splice variants (PDE4C-791, -426, -delta54, -delta109). PDE4C-delta54 and the 426-aa form are enzymatically active, and delta54 is sensitive to PDE4 inhibitors. The delta109 form lacks activity. Isoform expression is tissue-specific: delta54 only in testis, and the 5'-extended 791 form only in lung and G361 melanoma cells.

citation: Purification and physical characterization of cloned human cAMP phosphodiesterases PDE-4D and -4C (PMID: 9515166)
summary: Recombinant human PDE4C (61.4 kDa) was expressed in Sf9 cells and purified about 125-fold. Biophysical analysis showed PDE4C forms are highly asymmetric molecules that can form dimers.

citation: Hypoxia-conditioned BMSC exosomes improve short-term spinal cord injury outcomes via the miR-615-3p/PDE4C-mediated cAMP/PKA pathway (PMID: 41526970)
summary: miR-615-3p in hypoxic BMSC exosomes directly targets and suppresses PDE4C, activating cAMP/PKA signaling. This modulates calcium signaling and reduces mitochondrial calcium overload and ER stress in injured spinal neurons. In a mouse SCI model, exosome treatment downregulated PDE4C and improved functional recovery.

citation: Phosphodiesterase 4 inhibition synergizes with relaxin signaling to promote decidualization of human endometrial stromal cells (PMID: 14715868)
significance: significant upregulation (p-value not specified in abstract)
summary: PDE4C and PDE4D gene expression was significantly upregulated during in vitro decidualization of human endometrial stromal cells. PDE4 (rolipram-sensitive) activity is central to cAMP control, and PDE4 inhibition synergizes with relaxin to drive decidualization.

citation: Differential regulation of human antigen-specific Th1 and Th2 lymphocyte responses by isozyme selective cyclic nucleotide phosphodiesterase inhibitors (PMID: 9223593)
summary: Th1 clones showed reduced PDE4C expression, and lacked PDE4D, compared with Th2 clones. This differential PDE4 isoform expression may explain the greater sensitivity of Th2 cells to rolipram.

citation: Genetic loci for alcohol-related life events and substance-induced affective symptoms: indexing the 'dark side' of addiction (PMID: 30718457)
summary: Whole-genome sequencing association and rare-variant analysis found rare missense and splice-site variants in PDE4C associated with alcohol-related life events. The signal had converging evidence in American Indian and European American cohorts.

citation: Neuroprotective Effects of Qi Jing Wan and Its Active Ingredient Diosgenin Against Cognitive Impairment in Plateau Hypoxia (PMID: 40430556)
summary: In mouse models of plateau hypoxia, transcriptomics indicated that diosgenin protects cognitive function and alleviates hypoxic brain damage by regulating PDE4C expression.

citation: Expression and function of phosphodiesterases (PDEs) in the rat urinary bladder (PMID: 28687079)
summary: PDE4C mRNA was not detected in neonatal or adult rat urinary bladder, although PDE4A, 4B and 4D were expressed. This indicates a restricted tissue distribution for PDE4C.

citation: Levy et al. 2017 - Molecular and clinical delineation of 2p15p16.1 microdeletion syndrome (PMID: 28573701)
variant_detail: Heterozygous de novo 427 kb deletion at 2p16.1 (chr2:60624940-61051867) encompassing BCL11A and PAPOLG
phenotype: speech delay; autistic traits; motor stereotypies; brain structure abnormalities; no microcephaly
diagnostic_reason: De novo 427 kb deletion that includes BCL11A and PAPOLG. The phenotype is attributed to the contiguous genes in the deletion, not to PAPOLG alone.
center_country: France (Hôpital Robert Debré / Cochin / APHP, Paris)

citation: ASHG 2015 - Molecular and clinical delineation of the 2p15-16.1 microdeletion syndrome (Levy J, et al.)
variant_detail: Heterozygous de novo 427 kb deletion at 2p16.1 (chr2:60624940-61051867) containing BCL11A and PAPOLG
phenotype: speech delay; autistic traits; stereotyped behavior; no microcephaly
diagnostic_reason: De novo deletion detected by SNP-array that includes BCL11A and PAPOLG. It is not specific to PAPOLG.

citation: 2025 - SARS-CoV-2-Induced PAPOLG Contributes to Inflammation Response by Stabilizing NF-κB mRNA (PMID: 40607946)
summary: PAPOLG was upregulated in SARS-CoV-2-infected THP-1 macrophages. Knockdown promoted NF-κB mRNA degradation and lowered TNF-α and IL-6. Overexpression stabilized NF-κB mRNA and raised TNF-α and IL-6. Genes subject to alternative polyadenylation were enriched in immune pathways.

citation: Functional atlas of vertebrate viral RNA elements that stabilize RNA and enhance translation (PMID: 42594865)
summary: The viral element Pt1 from Potamipivirus directly recruits canonical poly(A) polymerases (PAPγ/PAPOLG and PAPα) to drive cytoplasmic polyadenylation and stabilize linear mRNA. This extends PAPγ function beyond nuclear, transcription-coupled pre-mRNA processing.

citation: Systematic analysis of the frequently amplified 2p15-p16.1 locus reveals PAPOLG as a potential proto-oncogene in follicular and transformed follicular lymphoma (PMID: 31410080)
significance: significant overexpression vs normal B-cells (p-value not given in abstract)
summary: 2p15-p16.1 amplification is associated with increased PAPOLG and BCL11A transcription in tFL. PAPOLG expression rose further after histological transformation and was significantly overexpressed in FL compared with normal B-cells. PAPOLG is proposed as a potential proto-oncogene.

citation: Comprehensive analysis of GSEC/miR-101-3p/SNX16/PAPOLG axis in hepatocellular carcinoma (PMID: 35482720)
significance: Risk model AUC 0.691, 0.623 and 0.626 at 1, 3 and 5 years
summary: PAPOLG is highly expressed in HCC and associated with poor prognosis. It is part of a predicted ceRNA axis (GSEC/miR-101-3p/SNX16/PAPOLG) linked to prognosis and to macrophage polarization/immune infiltration.

citation: Traka et al. 2013 - A diet rich in high-glucoraphanin broccoli interacts with genotype to reduce discordance in plasma metabolite profiles by modulating mitochondrial function (PMID: 23964055)
significance: PAPOLG genotype P<0.001; genotype × diet P<0.001
summary: SNPs in PAPOLG separated two metabolic phenotypes in the high-glucoraphanin broccoli arm. PAPOLG genotype and genotype × diet had significant effects on the plasma metabolome (lipids, amino acids, TCA intermediates, acylcarnitines). The diet reduced differences between genotypes, consistent with a role in mitochondrial function.

citation: A combined blood based gene expression and plasma protein abundance signature for diagnosis of epithelial ovarian cancer - OVCAD consortium (PMID: 23551967)
sample_size: 343 samples for the 13-gene panel; 224 EOC patients and 65 controls for the combined model
summary: PAPOLG was one of 13 leukocyte genes whose blood expression differed in epithelial ovarian cancer patients. Combined with plasma proteins, the signature discriminated EOC from controls.

citation: Oocyte quality and in vivo embryo survival after ovarian stimulation in nulliparous and multiparous rabbit does (PMID: 35724452)
significance: Differences among groups reported (p-value not given in abstract)
summary: PAPOL-G (and PAPOL-A, MATER, ZAR1) expression in rabbit oocytes differed among superovulation and parity groups. This links poly(A) polymerase gamma expression to oocyte competence and the oocyte-embryo transition.

citation: Analysis of differentially expressed microRNAs in bovine mammary epithelial cells treated with lipoteichoic acid (PMID: 35997417)
summary: PAPOLG was among the differentially expressed predicted targets of LTA-responsive miRNAs in bovine mammary epithelial cells. These targets were enriched in MAPK signalling and related pathways.

citation: ASHG 2011 - Refining the 2p15-p16 Microdeletion Syndrome
summary: PAPOLG lies within a 1.11 Mb 2p15-p16.1 deletion in a child with developmental delay, microcephaly and dysmorphism. It lies outside the narrowed critical region (KIAA1841, C2orf74, AHSA2, USP34), so it is not a leading candidate.

citation: A 7q31.33q32.1 microdeletion including LRRC4 and GRM8 is associated with severe intellectual disability and characteristics of autism (PMID: 28224041)
variant_detail: de novo 1.9-Mb heterozygous microdeletion at 7q31.33q32.1 encompassing LRRC4, GRM8 and 11 other genes
phenotype: severe intellectual disability; characteristics of autism
diagnostic_reason: de novo 1.9-Mb deletion; LRRC4 is a synaptic cell adhesion molecule related to autism, and its deletion is proposed to contribute to the phenotype (multigene deletion, so LRRC4 is not proven to be causal)

citation: Nonrandom occurrence of multiple de novo coding variants in a proband indicates the existence of an oligogenic model in autism (PMID: 31332282)
variant_detail: de novo coding variant(s) in LRRC4 (specific variants not given in abstract)
phenotype: autism spectrum disorder
diagnostic_reason: LRRC4 identified as a new ASD candidate gene with recurrent de novo variants (extreme DNVs: LoF or damaging missense) in a meta-analysis of ASD trios

citation: A Massively Parallel Screen of 5'UTR Mutations Identifies Variants Impacting Translation and Protein Production in Neurodevelopmental Disorder Genes (PMID: 37961498)
variant_detail: 5'UTR de novo variant(s) in LRRC4 from autism probands (specific variants not given in abstract)
phenotype: autism / neurodevelopmental disorder
diagnostic_reason: Variant altered translational activity in neurons in a massively parallel reporter assay (functional evidence)

citation: Approaches for identification of 5' UTR mutations impacting translation and protein production from neurodevelopmental disorder genes (PMID: 41344325)
variant_detail: 5'UTR variant(s) in LRRC4 from NDD families (specific variants not given in abstract)
phenotype: neurodevelopmental disorder / autism
diagnostic_reason: Variant altered translation in the MPRA assays (functional evidence)

citation: Lee et al. 2018 - NGL-2 Deletion Leads to Autistic-like Behaviors Responsive to NMDAR Modulation (PMID: 29949768)
phenotype: Suppressed NMDAR-dependent synaptic plasticity in the hippocampus; Mild social interaction deficits; Repetitive behaviors; Autistic-like behaviors rapidly improved by pharmacological NMDAR activation; NGL-2 associates with NMDARs via PSD-95-dependent and -independent mechanisms

citation: 2025 - LRRC4 enhances synaptic function and alleviates neuronal injury in high-fat diet mice (PMID: 41494607)
phenotype: Impaired synaptic plasticity; Cognitive impairment (Morris water maze, nest building); Further decreased PSD-95 expression in HFD-fed Lrrc4-/- mice; Decreased Bcl-2 and increased cleaved caspase-3 and BAX in hippocampus of HFD Lrrc4-/- mice; Exacerbated neuronal injury and apoptosis; Overexpression of LRRC4 rescued behavioral abnormalities, increased dendritic branching, and strengthened synaptic transmission in HFD mice

citation: 2021 - LRRC4 functions as a neuron-protective role in experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (PMID: 33932995)
phenotype: Accelerated and exacerbated EAE disease progression; More severe myelin degeneration in the spinal cord; Increased leukocyte infiltration into the spinal cord; Elevated Rab7b and NF-κB p65; Increased IL-6 and IFN-γ, decreased TNF-α; Stronger Th1 immune response; AAV-LRRC4 expression alleviated EAE symptoms and protected neurons

citation: 2023 - Whole genome sequencing identifies genetic variants associated with neurogenic inflammation in rosacea (PMID: 37402769)
phenotype: Knock-in of a recurrent human Lrrc4 mutation causes rosacea-like skin inflammation; Excessive vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP) release by peripheral neurons

citation: LRRC4 Deficiency Drives Premature Ovarian Insufficiency by Disrupting Metabolic Homeostasis in Granulosa Cells (PMID: 40317712)
summary: LRRC4 is expressed in ovarian granulosa cells and supports folliculogenesis and ovarian reserve. LRRC4 deficiency causes defective oocyte maturation, follicular atresia and POI. LRRC4 promotes K48-linked ubiquitin degradation of YAP, which balances mitochondrial fission/fusion, limits mitophagy and maintains aerobic respiration/glycolysis. Targeting LRRC4 normalized follicular development in POI model mice.

citation: LRRC4 mediates the formation of circular RNA CD44 to inhibit GBM cell proliferation (PMID: 34631278)
summary: LRRC4 interacts with the RNA-binding protein SAM68 and blocks SAM68 binding to CD44 pre-mRNA, which promotes circCD44 biogenesis. circCD44 sponges miR-326 and miR-330-5p to regulate SMAD6, defining an LRRC4/SAM68/circCD44/miR-326/miR-330-5p/SMAD6 axis. circCD44 re-expression suppressed GBM proliferation, colony formation, invasion and in vivo tumor growth.

citation: LRRC4 Suppresses E-Cadherin-Dependent Collective Cell Invasion and Metastasis in Epithelial Ovarian Cancer (PMID: 32117780)
summary: LRRC4 binds the cSH2 domain of PIK3R1 and inhibits PIK3R1 activity without disrupting PIK3R1–PIK3CA binding. This inhibits AKT/GSK3β/β-catenin signaling and E-cadherin-dependent collective invasion and metastasis. LRRC4 is low in HGSC and metastasis, and AAV9-LRRC4 reduced metastasis in an orthotopic xenograft model.

citation: LRRC4 functions as a neuron-protective role in experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (PMID: 33932995)
summary: LRRC4 is mainly expressed in spinal cord neurons and is decreased in EAE mice. LRRC4-/- mice had worse EAE, with more demyelination, leukocyte infiltration and a stronger Th1 response. Loss of LRRC4 raised Rab7b and NF-κB p65, and AAV-LRRC4 overexpression alleviated disease.

citation: Expression and functional characterization of LRRC4, a novel brain-specific member of the LRR superfamily (PMID: 15967442)
summary: LRRC4 expression is restricted to normal adult brain in human and mouse, is developmentally regulated, and is down-regulated in brain tumors and U251MG cells. Induction in a Tet-on system caused late G1 delay, with changes in p21, p27, Cdk2, PCNA and p-ERK1/2.

citation: Expression and clinical significance of LRRC4 in benign and malignant nasopharyngeal diseases (PMID: 26662436)
summary: By immunohistochemistry, LRRC4 was strongly expressed in chronic nasopharyngitis (82.1%) and precancerous lesions (81.8%) but weakly in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (10%). Loss of LRRC4 expression is a major feature of NPC and did not differ by stage or grade.

citation: LRRC4 inhibits glioma cell growth and invasion through a miR-185-dependent pathway (PMID: 22834685)
summary: LRRC4 upregulates miR-185, which targets CDC42 and RhoA (with indirect effects on VEGFA), to suppress glioma cell invasion. Low LRRC4 and miR-185 correlate with poor glioma patient outcome.

citation: LRRC4 inhibits glioblastoma cell proliferation, migration, and angiogenesis by downregulating pleiotropic cytokine expression and responses (PMID: 17541939)
summary: Stable LRRC4 expression in U251 cells reduced cytokines and their receptors, K-RAS expression, and phosphorylation of c-Raf, ERK, AKT, NF-κBp65, p70S6K and PKC. It also reduced AP-1, NF-κB and CyclinD1 activation, indicating inhibition of RTK signaling. LRRC4 blunted cytokine-driven proliferation and migration and impaired VEGF-induced endothelial tube formation.

citation: MicroRNA-381 Favors Repair of Nerve Injury Through Regulation of the SDF-1/CXCR4 Signaling Pathway via LRRC4 in Acute Cerebral Ischemia after Cerebral Lymphatic Blockage (PMID: 29669322)
summary: LRRC4 is a target of miR-381 in a rat MCAO/cerebral lymphatic blockage model. miR-381 upregulation lowers LRRC4 and activates SDF-1/CXCR4 signaling (with increased pERK, Slit2, VEGF). This reduced infarct volume, apoptosis and inflammation and promoted nerve repair.

citation: LRRC4 Orchestrates AP2A1-Containing Clathrin-Coated Vesicles to Disrupt Mitochondrial Cristae and Restrict Glioblastoma Progression (PMID: 42439431)
summary: LRRC4 is a Golgi-anchored tumor suppressor that engages AP2A1-containing clathrin-coated vesicles and redirects them to the inner mitochondrial membrane. This disrupts the MICOS complex, suppresses Mic60, collapses cristae, impairs oxidative phosphorylation and triggers excessive mitophagy. The result is suppressed GBM proliferation and invasion in vitro and in xenografts.

citation: Yamada et al. 2020 - A recurrent PJA1 variant in trigonocephaly and neurodevelopmental disorders (PMID: 32530565)
variant_detail: De novo truncation variant in ZMYND8 (exact nucleotide/protein notation not given in abstract)
phenotype: Neurodevelopmental disorder (individual phenotype not specified in abstract)
diagnostic_reason: De novo truncation variant identified by exome sequencing in a cohort of NDD patients (ZMYND8 proposed as novel candidate NDD gene)

citation: RACK7 Interacts with PRC2 Complex to Regulate Astrocyte Development (PMID: 40125808)
phenotype: Rack7 (Zmynd8)-deficient mice exhibit overt developmental defects; Aberrant astrocyte development; Deletion of Rack7 in astrocytes markedly decreases genome-wide H3K27me3 chromatin localization; Altered SUZ12 and H3K27me3 genomic localization; Overactivation of Wnt signaling and astrocyte differentiation genes

citation: Zinc finger MYND-type containing 8 promotes tumour angiogenesis via induction of vascular endothelial growth factor-A expression (PMID: 25117453)
phenotype: In vivo ZMYND8 knockdown suppressed angiogenesis in zebrafish prostate cancer xenografts; ZMYND8 induced vegfa mRNA expression selectively in prostate cancer xenografts; ZMYND8 overexpression enhanced angiogenesis

citation: ZMYND8 Expression in Breast Cancer Cells Blocks T-Lymphocyte Surveillance to Promote Tumor Growth (PMID: 33148660)
phenotype: ZMYND8 KO tumor cells showed increased micronuclei and DNA damage, with cGAS-STING/NF-κB activation and IFNβ/ISG induction in tumors; Increased CD4+ and CD8+ T cell infiltration; Tumor growth inhibition in syngeneic mice, attenuated by CD4/CD8 depletion, anti-IFNAR1 antibody, and in Rag1 KO mice
knockout_type: other (ZMYND8 knockout in breast cancer cells implanted in syngeneic mice)

citation: Validation of ZMYND8 as a new treatment target in hepatocellular carcinoma (PMID: 34462784)
phenotype: ZMYND8 knockdown in HCC cells significantly reduced tumor growth in a nude mouse xenograft model; Knockdown reduced migration and invasion and promoted apoptosis in vitro
significance: significant reduction in xenograft tumor growth (p-value not given in abstract)

citation: De Novo ZMYND8 variants result in an autosomal dominant neurodevelopmental disorder with cardiac malformations (PMID: 35916866)
sample_size: 11 unrelated individuals with variants; Drosophila knockdown model
summary: Neuronal knockdown of the Drosophila ZMYND8 ortholog decreased habituation learning, consistent with a role in cognition. De novo variants were found in 11 individuals with intellectual disability. PWWP-domain missense variants abolish the Drebrin interaction, and MYND-domain variants disrupt the GATAD2A interaction. ZMYND8 is broadly expressed in brain, with highest expression in early brain development.

citation: Positive Regulation of Transcription by Human ZMYND8 through Its Association with P-TEFb Complex (PMID: 30134174)
summary: ZMYND8 binds CyclinT1 directly to form a minimal ZMYND8-P-TEFb complex that activates target genes and is needed for ATRA-mediated neuronal differentiation. Through its coiled-coil domain, the ZMYND8 homodimer associates with P-TEFb, whereas the monomer associates with CHD4 of the NuRD repressor complex.

citation: ZMYND8 suppresses MAPT213 LncRNA transcription to promote neuronal differentiation (PMID: 36064715)
summary: In ATRA-differentiated neuronal cells, ZMYND8 promotes expression of the canonical MAPT coding isoform and epigenetically silences the non-coding MAPT213 isoform. ZMYND8 deletion raised MAPT213, and ectopic MAPT213 repressed the MAPT coding transcript.

citation: ZMYND8 Is a Regulator of Sonic Hedgehog Signaling in ATRA-Mediated Differentiation of Neuroblastoma Cells (PMID: 38804064)
summary: ZMYND8 knockout reduced SHH pathway genes GLI1 and PTCH1 during ATRA-induced differentiation. ZMYND8 co-occupies their promoters with RNA pol II S5P and counteracts the SMO inhibitor cyclopamine, enhancing neurite formation.

citation: ZMYND8 mediated liquid condensates spatiotemporally decommission the latent super-enhancers during macrophage polarization (PMID: 34764296)
summary: ZMYND8 forms liquid condensates with acetylated NF-κB/p65, is redistributed onto latent super-enhancers, and recruits LSD1 to silence them and restrain macrophage inflammation. Mutations that solidify the condensates abolish this function.

citation: The Chromatin Reader ZMYND8 Regulates Igh Enhancers to Promote Immunoglobulin Class Switch Recombination (PMID: 30293785)
summary: In B cells ZMYND8 binds promoters and super-enhancers, including the Igh 3'RR. ZMYND8 loss increases polymerase loading at the 3'RR, decreases acceptor region transcription, and impairs class switch recombination and somatic hypermutation.

citation: Targeting ZMYND8 unleashes IL-2 signalling to override T cell exhaustion (PMID: 42778612)
summary: In vivo single-cell CRISPR screens showed ZMYND8 is induced by chronic antigen and represses p300-mediated Il2ra enhancer activity, which limits IL-2R-STAT5 signalling and promotes terminal exhaustion. ZMYND8-deficient CD8+ T cells had improved antiviral and antitumour function.

citation: Targeting the histone reader ZMYND8 inhibits antiandrogen-induced neuroendocrine tumor transdifferentiation of prostate cancer (PMID: 40102673)
summary: A CRISPR-Cas9 screen combined with scRNA-seq showed ZMYND8 drives NEPC transdifferentiation. ZMYND8 is upregulated by ASCL1, and FOXM1 stabilizes its chromatin binding. It interacts with SWI/SNF, and the inhibitor iZMYND8-34 blocks NEPC development. Zmynd8 ablation prevents NEPC.

citation: ZMYND8 protects breast cancer stem cells against oxidative stress and ferroptosis through activation of NRF2 (PMID: 38488001)
summary: ZMYND8 stabilizes NRF2 through KEAP1 silencing and recruits NRF2 to antioxidant gene promoters, reducing ROS and ferroptosis in ALDHhi breast cancer stem cells. NRF2 in turn controls ZMYND8 expression, forming a positive feedback loop.

citation: USP7 deubiquitinates epigenetic reader ZMYND8 to promote breast cancer cell migration and invasion (PMID: 39128723)
summary: USP7 binds the ZMYND8 PBP domain and removes FBXW7-catalyzed polyubiquitin at K1034, stabilizing ZMYND8. This raises transcription of ZEB1 and VEGFA and promotes migration and invasion. USP7 and ZMYND8 protein levels correlate in breast cancer tissue.

citation: Anonymous et al. 2022 - de novo variant calling identifies cancer mutation signatures in the 1000 Genomes Project (PMID: 36054329)
variant_detail: Excess of protein-coding de novo variants in IGLL5 in 1000 Genomes LCL-derived WGS data; specific variants not given in abstract; likely cell line (somatic hypermutation) artifacts
diagnostic_reason: Statistically significant excess of protein-coding DNVs in IGLL5, a gene involved in B-cell lymphomas; interpreted as likely LCL cell-line artifacts rather than pathogenic germline variants

citation: A discovery resource of rare copy number variations in individuals with autism spectrum disorder (PMID: 23275889)
variant_detail: 22q11.23 gain (~656 kb), maternally inherited, encompassing RAB36, FBXW4P1, RTDR1, GNAZ, MIR650, IGLL5, BCR (heterozygous copy gain)
phenotype: Autism spectrum disorder
diagnostic_reason: Rare inherited CNV in an ASD case detected by CGH array; IGLL5 only one of several genes in the interval, not specifically implicated as causal

citation: IGLL5 controlled by super-enhancer affects cell survival and MYC expression in mature B-cell lymphoma (PMID: 38444524)
summary: Two mature B-cell lymphoma cell lines expressed IGLL5 mRNA containing the Cλ1 segment. JQ1 (BET inhibitor) treatment down-regulated IGLL5, indicating super-enhancer control. IGLL5 knockdown induced cell death with reduced MYC expression, suggesting a role in survival and MYC regulation.

citation: A multiple myeloma-specific capture sequencing platform discovers novel translocations and frequent, risk-associated point mutations in IGLL5 (PMID: 29563506)
summary: IGLL5 was recurrently mutated in 18% of multiple myeloma tumors. The mutations were mutually exclusive with RAS mutations and associated with increased risk of disease progression. Novel IGLL5/IGH translocations were found in two samples.

citation: Identification of hub genes and therapeutic drugs in rheumatoid arthritis patients (PMID: 33604823)
sample_size: GEO datasets GSE55235 and GSE12021 plus RA patient and healthy control blood samples
summary: IGLL5 was identified as an upregulated hub gene in RA synovial expression datasets, in the context of enrichment for B cell receptor signalling and immune response. qRT-PCR confirmed its overexpression in RA patient blood versus healthy controls. hsa-miR-1185-5p and hsa-miR-3679-5p were predicted to regulate it.

citation: Gene expression profiling of periodontitis-affected gingival tissue by spatial transcriptomics (PMID: 29921943)
significance: significantly up-regulated (specific p-values not given in abstract)
summary: IGLL5 was the most up-regulated gene in inflamed versus non-inflamed gingival connective tissue, together with SSR4, MZB1 and XBP1. RT-qPCR confirmed higher expression in periodontitis patients than in healthy controls, and protein expression was supported by immunohistochemistry.

citation: IGLL5 is correlated with tumor-infiltrating immune cells in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (PMID: 33449444)
summary: In TCGA ccRCC, IGLL5 was the single gene overlapping between the PPI network and Cox regression analyses. Its expression correlated positively with three types of tumor-infiltrating immune cells and may be a prognostic biomarker.

citation: Lineage-negative lymphoma with a helper innate lymphoid cell phenotype (PMID: 31522287)
summary: Next-generation sequencing of an aggressive lineage-negative lymphoma with a helper ILC phenotype identified a novel IGLV2-14/IGLL5 fusion. This adds IGLL5 to the list of genes involved in rearrangements in hematologic malignancy.

citation: Lymphoma driver mutations at the root of somatic evolution of nerve-damaging autoantibodies in myelin associated glycoprotein neuropathy (PMID: 40915157)
summary: Single-cell DNA and RNA analysis of MAG-autoantibody B cell clones found sub-clonal branches with somatic mutations in IGLL5, along with CXCR4 and BTG2, acquired after MYD88 L265P. This implicates IGLL5 mutation in the clonal evolution of autoreactive B cells.

citation: Comprehensive characterization of driver genes in diffuse large B cell lymphoma (PMID: 32565964)
summary: Computational driver-gene analysis identified IGLL5 as the most frequently mutated gene in DLBCL, ahead of MLL2, BTG2, B2M, PIM1 and CARD11.

citation: Dynamic landscape of m6A modifications and related post-transcriptional events in muscle-invasive bladder cancer (PMID: 39380003)
sample_size: 3 paired MIBC tumor/normal samples plus validation pairs
summary: Nanopore direct-RNA sequencing identified a novel m6A site in the IGLL5 3'UTR in MIBC tumors. The site showed a lower m6A methylation ratio, elongated poly(A) tails and biased transcript usage, suggesting post-transcriptional regulation of IGLL5.
