citation: Molecular biomarkers screened by next-generation RNA sequencing for non-sentinel lymph node status prediction in breast cancer patients with metastatic sentinel lymph nodes (PMID: 26311227)
summary: RNA-seq of sentinel lymph node metastases found that IGLL5 was the most frequently fused gene among 10 gene fusions in the NSLN-positive group.

citation: Mutations of the histone linker H1-4 in neurodevelopmental disorders and functional characterization of neurons expressing C-terminus frameshift mutant H1.4 (PMID: 34788807)
variant_detail: Novel C-terminal frameshift indels in H1-4 (specific notations not given in abstract); the abstract states they create the shared frameshift and truncated H1.4 with an abnormal C-terminal frameshifted tail (H1.4 CFT)
phenotype: intellectual disability; hypotonia; anxiety; autism spectrum disorder; vision problems; bone abnormalities; dysmorphic facies; features consistent with Rahman syndrome
diagnostic_reason: C-terminal frameshift variants had clinical features consistent with prior Rahman syndrome reports, which strengthens support for the pathogenicity of H1.4 CFT. Neuronal expression of H1.4 CFT altered about 400 genes and reduced neuronal activity.

citation: Mutations of the histone linker H1-4 in neurodevelopmental disorders and functional characterization of neurons expressing C-terminus frameshift mutant H1.4 (PMID: 34788807)
variant_detail: Novel N-terminus H1-4 variant(s) (details not given in abstract)
phenotype: neurodevelopmental disorder (details not given in abstract)
diagnostic_reason: C-terminal frameshift variants had clinical features consistent with prior Rahman syndrome reports, which strengthens support for the pathogenicity of H1.4 CFT. Neuronal expression of H1.4 CFT altered about 400 genes and reduced neuronal activity.

citation: Epigenetics and autism spectrum disorder: A report of an autism case with mutation in H1 linker histone HIST1H1E and literature review (PMID: 29704315)
variant_detail: HIST1H1E (H1-4) c.435dupC, p.Thr146Hisfs*50
phenotype: autism spectrum disorder; intellectual disability
diagnostic_reason: De novo frameshift at the 3' end of the gene, found on clinical whole exome sequencing. It truncates the positively charged C-terminus, and expression studies showed reduced protein expression, supporting haploinsufficiency/loss of function. Other published HIST1H1E cases support causality.

citation: Journal article 2025/2026 - The linker histone H1.4 condenses chromatin in maturing postmitotic neurons (PMID: 42619895)
phenotype: Developmental maturation of chromatin compaction in cerebellar granule neurons is disrupted in H1f2/H1f4 double knockout mice; H1.4 accumulates in heterochromatin over the course of neuronal maturation; Epitope-tagged H1f4 knock-in mice show robust H1.4 expression throughout the brain, including in mature post-mitotic neurons
knockout_type: full knockout (H1f2/H1f4 double knockout); also epitope-tagged H1f4 knock-in

citation: Spermatogenesis proceeds normally in mice without linker histone H1t (PMID: 10933220)
phenotype: H1t-null mice developed normally with no anatomic abnormalities; Spermatogenesis and testicular morphology were unchanged; H1.1, H1.2 and H1.4 gene expression was enhanced during spermatogenesis in H1t-deficient mice (compensatory upregulation)
knockout_type: full knockout (of H1t, a different H1 gene; H1-4 was not knocked out but its expression was measured in the H1t-null mice)

citation: Yusufova et al. 2021 - Histone H1 loss drives lymphoma by disrupting 3D chromatin architecture (PMID: 33299181)
summary: H1-4 (H1E) is one of the B-cell lymphoma-recurrently mutated H1 isoforms, and the lymphoma-associated H1 alleles act as driver mutations. Combined loss of H1c and H1e in mice decompacts chromatin, shifts H3K36me2/H3K27me3 states and derepresses stem cell genes. This gave germinal centre B cells enhanced fitness and drove aggressive lymphomas, establishing H1 as a tumour suppressor.

citation: Sarg/Medrzycki-type study: Sancho et al. 2008 - Depletion of human histone H1 variants uncovers specific roles in gene expression and cell growth (PMID: 18927631)
summary: Inducible shRNA knockdown of H1.4 in T47D breast cancer cells caused cell death. This was the first evidence that an H1 variant is essential for survival in a human cell type. Microarrays showed that each H1 variant knockdown alters a distinct gene subset, without compensation by other variants.

citation: Kuo et al. 2017 - Mutations in Epigenetic Regulation Genes Are a Major Cause of Overgrowth with Intellectual Disability (PMID: 28475857)
sample_size: 710 individuals with OGID (353 with a causal mutation)
significance: overlap with height GWAS genes p=6.84e-8; overlap with cancer driver genes p=1.75e-14
summary: Pathogenic HIST1H1E (H1.4) mutations were identified in individuals with overgrowth and intellectual disability. The mutations are predicted to truncate the C-terminal domain and reduce net charge, impairing neutralisation of linker DNA and DNA/protein binding. HIST1H1E was one of six epigenetic regulator genes accounting for 44% of cases.

citation: Linker histone H1.4 phosphorylation study - K-Ras(G12V/Y40C)-PI3K/AKT pathway regulates H1.4(S35ph) through PKA in osteosarcoma (PMID: 31126199)
summary: In MG-63 osteosarcoma cells, RasG12V/Y40C-PI3K/AKT signalling lowers H1.4 S35 phosphorylation by downregulating PKA and upregulating MDM2. Overexpressing the phosphomimetic H1.4S35E reduced viability, colony formation and migration, opposing Ras effects.

citation: Ras-ERK signalling represses H1.4 phosphorylation at serine 36 to promote NSCLC cell growth and migration (PMID: 31184227)
summary: Ras-ERK signalling represses H1.4 S36 phosphorylation through MDM2-dependent degradation of PKA in NSCLC cells (NCI-H2126, A549). H1.4S36ph acts as a tumour suppressor: its overexpression reduced viability, colony formation, migration and invasion, caused S-phase arrest, and modulated transcription of Ras downstream genes.

citation: Linker histone H1.2 and H1.4 affect the neutrophil lineage determination (PMID: 32391789)
summary: A genome-wide CRISPR/Cas9 screen in PLB-985 cells and H1 subtype knockouts showed that loss of H1.2 and H1.4 induces an eosinophil-like transcriptional program. H1.4 therefore negatively regulates eosinophil-biased differentiation and supports neutrophil lineage commitment. H1 subtypes also affected the eosinophil bias of murine bone marrow stem cells.

citation: Linker Histone H1.4 Inhibits the Growth, Migration and EMT Process of NSCLC by Regulating ERK1/2 Expression (PMID: 38472566)
summary: H1.4 overexpression in A549 and H1299 cells inhibited viability, migration, invasion and EMT, while shRNA knockdown promoted them. H1.4 binds the ERK1/2 promoter and acts as a transcriptional repressor. ERK re-expression largely rescued the H1.4 effects.

citation: CYP1B1 promotes PARPi-resistance via histone H1.4 interaction and increased chromatin accessibility in ovarian cancer (PMID: 39395328)
summary: LC-MS identified H1.4 as an interactor of CYP1B1 in PARPi-resistant A2780-OlaR ovarian cancer cells. H1.4 downregulation was associated with increased chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq) and higher viability after Olaparib treatment.

citation: A Rahman Syndrome mutation in histone H1.4 disrupts chromatin compaction and phase separation (PMID: 42173878)
summary: A Rahman syndrome frameshift mutation truncates the H1.4 C-terminal domain and reduces its positive charge. Mutant H1.4-bound hexanucleosome arrays are more extended, with greater linker DNA accessibility and reduced liquid-liquid and liquid-solid phase separation, resembling arrays without linker histone. The mutant also shows increased mobility in cell nuclei, indicating weaker chromatin association.

citation: CMAHP promotes metastasis by reducing ubiquitination of Snail and inducing angiogenesis via GM-CSF overexpression in gastric cancer (PMID: 34716430)
summary: The pseudogene CMAHP interacts with histone H1.4 and promotes histone acetylation, which enhances c-Jun and RelA (p65) expression in gastric cancer cells. This drives GM-CSF transactivation, angiogenesis and metastasis.

citation: Improved neuron protection following cortical injury in the absence of Semaphorin4B (PMID: 36531136)
phenotype: Reduced neuronal cell death after cortical injury; More surviving neurons near the injury site; Wild-type neurons survive better on glial cultures from Sema4B knockout mice than on heterozygous cultures; Conditioned medium from Sema4B knockout glia increases neuronal survival, indicating a glia-dependent secreted factor; Altered astrocyte activation after injury

citation: Astrocyte-to-microglia communication via Sema4B-Plexin-B2 modulates injury-induced reactivity of microglia (PMID: 38781210)
phenotype: Attenuated cytokine expression after cortical stab wound injury in Sema4B-/- mice; Altered microglia/macrophage reactivity after injury; Sema4B-/- astrocytes attenuate injury-induced microglia reactivity compared with Sema4B+/- astrocytes; Microglia-specific Plexin-B2-/- mice show reduced microglial/macrophage reactivity and neuronal cell death after injury, similar to Sema4B-/- mice; Sema4B/Plexin-B2 double heterozygous mice show reduced microglial/macrophage reactivity after injury
knockout_type: full knockout (Sema4B-/-), heterozygous (Sema4B/Plexin-B2 double heterozygous), and microglia/macrophage-specific conditional Plexin-B2 knockout

citation: Nakagawa et al. 2011 - Identification of semaphorin 4B as a negative regulator of basophil-mediated immune responses (PMID: 21270411)
phenotype: Markedly increased serum IgE levels; Normal lymphocyte and dendritic cell functions; Enhanced basophil-mediated memory IgE production, abolished by anti-FcεRIα antibody treatment; Loss of T cell-derived Sema4B removes suppression of basophil-mediated Th2 skewing

citation: Enhanced Protein Synthesis and Hippocampus-Dependent Memory via Inhibition of YTHDF2-Mediated m(6)A mRNA Degradation (PMID: 40959883)
phenotype: Reducing the YTHDF2 target Sema4B in the hippocampus reversed the enhanced hippocampus-dependent memory seen in YTHDF2 conditional knockout mice; YTHDF2 loss produced enhanced synaptic transmission, improved learning and memory, and increased activity-dependent protein synthesis
knockout_type: knockdown of Sema4B in hippocampus (in forebrain-specific YTHDF2 conditional knockout mice)

citation: Sema4B-Plexin-B2 - Astrocyte-to-microglia communication via Sema4B-Plexin-B2 modulates injury-induced reactivity of microglia (PMID: 38781210)
summary: Astrocytic Sema4B acts as a ligand for Plexin-B2 on microglia/macrophages and enhances their reactivity after cortical injury. Sema4B-/-, microglia-specific Plexin-B2-/- and Sema4B/Plexin-B2 double-heterozygous mice all show attenuated reactivity, placing both genes in the same signaling pathway.

citation: Improved neuron protection following cortical injury in the absence of Semaphorin4B (PMID: 36531136)
summary: Sema4B is mostly expressed by astrocytes in cortex. Sema4B knockout mice show reduced neuronal death after cortical injury. Wild-type neurons survive better on Sema4B-null glia or in their conditioned medium, indicating a glia-dependent, secreted-factor mechanism. Sema4B protein applied directly to neurons has no effect.

citation: Astrogliosis Induced by Brain Injury Is Regulated by Sema4B Phosphorylation (PMID: 26464987)
summary: Sema4B-deficient mice and cultured Sema4B-/- astrocytes show reduced astrocyte proliferation and altered activation after injury. The Sema4B ectodomain acts as an antagonist rather than a rescuing ligand. Its effects depend on phosphorylation of the intracellular domain at Ser825, so Sema4B functions as an astrocyte receptor.

citation: Enhanced Protein Synthesis and Hippocampus-Dependent Memory via Inhibition of YTHDF2-Mediated m(6)A mRNA Degradation (PMID: 40959883)
summary: SEMA4B is a downstream target of YTHDF2-mediated m6A mRNA decay in hippocampal neurons. Forebrain YTHDF2 loss stabilizes m6A mRNAs and enhances memory. Reducing SEMA4B in the hippocampus reverses the enhanced memory in the conditional knockout mice.

citation: Identification of semaphorin 4B as a negative regulator of basophil-mediated immune responses (PMID: 21270411)
summary: Sema4B is expressed in T and B cells. Sema4B-/- mice have elevated serum IgE and enhanced basophil-mediated memory IgE production. Recombinant Sema4B inhibits basophil IL-4 and IL-6 production, and T cell-derived Sema4B at T cell-basophil contact sites suppresses Th2 skewing.

citation: Semaphorin 4B is an ADAM17-cleaved adipokine that inhibits adipocyte differentiation and thermogenesis (PMID: 37121509)
summary: Proteomics identified SEMA4B as an ADAM17-shed adipokine whose expression is regulated by thermogenic cues. Cleaved SEMA4B acts in an autocrine manner in brown adipocytes to repress adipogenesis, thermogenesis and lipid catabolism genes.

citation: Semaphorin4B is elevated in rheumatoid arthritis and enhances the inflammatory phenotype of macrophages and fibroblast-like synoviocytes (PMID: 40598553)
summary: Sema4B is higher in RA synovial tissue and RA FLS than in OA FLS, and inflammatory stimuli induce its expression. Sema4B promotes FLS migration and invasion, and enhances TNF-α/LPS-induced IL-6, IL-8, TNF-α, CCL-2, MMP-1 and MMP-3 production. In FLS this effect is mediated by PlexinB2, as shown by siRNA knockdown.

citation: CLCP1 interacts with semaphorin 4B and regulates motility of lung cancer cells (PMID: 17213806)
summary: A phage display screen and immunoprecipitation showed that SEMA4B (Sema domain) physically interacts with CLCP1. SEMA4B enhances ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of CLCP1, which regulates lung cancer cell motility.

citation: SEMA4B inhibits growth of non-small cell lung cancer in vitro and in vivo (PMID: 25746385)
summary: SEMA4B overexpression decreased NSCLC (A549, Calu-3) growth in vitro and in xenografts, while inhibition increased growth. SEMA4B suppresses PI3K/Akt signaling, causing FoxO1 nuclear retention and p21 induction, which changes proliferation but not apoptosis.

citation: Hypoxia and hypoxia-inducible factor 1 repress SEMA4B expression to promote non-small cell lung cancer invasion (PMID: 24474252)
summary: Hypoxia downregulates SEMA4B in NSCLC lines. SEMA4B is a direct HIF-1 target: HIF-1α binds a hypoxia-responsive element in the SEMA4B gene (luciferase reporter) and represses it. Ectopic SEMA4B abolishes hypoxia-induced invasion.

citation: Expanding the phenotype of NEDAMSS with a psychiatric perspective: analysis of a new case, and a systematic review of the literature (PMID: 39031186)
variant_detail: Not specified in abstract (novel case plus 32 previously reported NEDAMSS cases)
phenotype: neurodevelopmental regression; abnormal movements; loss of speech; seizures; catatonia; affective disorders; psychotic symptoms; developmental disorders; motor symptoms improved with lorazepam after catatonia diagnosis
diagnostic_reason: Pathogenic IRF2BPL variants causing NEDAMSS; variant-level details not given in abstract

citation: ASHG 2019 - PgmNr 3148: Unravelling the mechanism underlying IRF2BPL in a neurodevelopmental disorder with regression, abnormal movements, loss of speech, and seizures

citation: ASHG 2019 - PgmNr 3148: Unravelling the mechanism underlying IRF2BPL in a neurodevelopmental disorder with regression, abnormal movements, loss of speech, and seizures

phenotype: seizures; global developmental delay; autism spectrum disorder; milder phenotype
diagnostic_reason: De novo variants; nonsense variants behaved as severe loss-of-function alleles in Drosophila and missense variants gave milder phenotypes
center_country: Duke University (Shashi) and Baylor College of Medicine/Texas Children's (Bellen, Wangler), USA

variant_detail: De novo truncating variants (specific changes not given)
phenotype: neurological regression after initial normal development; gait deterioration; loss of intentional movements; dysarthria; loss of speech; movement disorder; seizures; loss of fine motor skills
diagnostic_reason: De novo truncating variants; Drosophila functional studies used to assess variants of uncertain significance

knockout_type: other (CRISPR crispants, F0 mosaic disruption of irf2bpl)

citation: Zhang et al. 2022 - N(6)-methyladenosine-modified circRNA RERE modulates osteoarthritis by regulating β-catenin ubiquitination and degradation (PMID: 35733354)
phenotype: Irf2bpl knockdown reduced the chondroprotective effect of circRere overexpression in DMM-induced osteoarthritis; the detrimental effects of sh-Irf2bpl were counteracted by the β-catenin inhibitor ICG-001
knockout_type: knockdown (AAV-sh-Irf2bpl intra-articular injection in the DMM osteoarthritis model)

citation: Marcogliese et al. 2022 - Loss of IRF2BPL impairs neuronal maintenance through excess Wnt signaling (PMID: 35044823)
summary: In Drosophila and zebrafish, IRF2BPL and its ortholog Pits repress Wnt transcription. Neuronal loss of Pits raises wingless levels and causes axonal loss, and Wg inhibition is neuroprotective. Zebrafish irf2bpl loss increases wnt1 signaling, and patient astrocytes show increased WNT1. IRF2BPL physically and genetically interacts with the Wnt antagonist CKIα.

citation: Ginevrino/Tsai et al. 2022 - Mechanisms of IRF2BPL-related disorders and identification of a potential therapeutic strategy (PMID: 36476864)
summary: In patient fibroblast-derived astrocytes and neurons, full-length IRF2BPL is nuclear. Truncated NEDAMSS variants sequester wild-type protein to the cytoplasm and cause aggregation. Patient astrocytes fail to support neuronal survival and show mitochondrial and respiratory dysfunction, which CuATSM rescues. In flies, truncated IRF2BPL causes cytoplasmic accumulation of full-length protein, and heterozygous Pits truncations cause progressive motor defects that CuATSM ameliorates.

citation: Marcogliese et al. 2018 - IRF2BPL Is Associated with Neurological Phenotypes (PMID: 30057031)
summary: The fly ortholog pits is broadly expressed, including in the nervous system. Complete loss of pits is lethal early in development, and neuronal RNAi knockdown causes neurodegeneration. Patient nonsense variants act as severe loss-of-function alleles in flies, while missense variants give a range of phenotypes.

citation: Gastric cancer study 2018 - Forkhead Box F2 Suppresses Gastric Cancer through a Novel FOXF2-IRF2BPL-β-Catenin Signaling Axis (PMID: 29374064)
summary: FOXF2 directly binds the IRF2BPL promoter and induces its transcription. IRF2BPL, an E3 ligase, interacts with β-catenin and increases its ubiquitination and degradation, which blunts Wnt signaling in gastric cancer cells.

citation: 2022 - N(6)-methyladenosine-modified circRNA RERE modulates osteoarthritis by regulating β-catenin ubiquitination and degradation (PMID: 35733354)
summary: circRERE sponges miR-195-5p to upregulate IRF2BPL, which promotes β-catenin ubiquitination and degradation in chondrocytes. In a mouse DMM osteoarthritis model, AAV-sh-Irf2bpl worsened OA and the β-catenin inhibitor ICG-001 reversed this effect.

citation: 2025 - IRF2BPL inhibits proliferation, migration and invasion of osteosarcoma cells by inhibiting FOSL2-mediated PI3K/AKT pathway activation (PMID: 40834975)
summary: IRF2BPL is downregulated in osteosarcoma and correlates with patient survival. Overexpression suppresses proliferation, migration and invasion in vitro and in xenografts, and silencing enhances them. It acts by promoting ubiquitin-mediated degradation of FOSL2, thereby inhibiting PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling.

citation: 2025 - IRF2BPL transcriptionally regulates IGFBP2 to promote tumor progression and suppresses immune cell infiltration in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (PMID: 41413713)
summary: IRF2BPL is highly expressed in ESCC cells and acts as a transcriptional activator of IGFBP2, promoting tumor progression in vitro and in vivo and reducing immune cell infiltration. ONC201 impedes the progression driven by the IRF2BPL-IGFBP2 axis.

citation: 2021 - Identification and Functional Characterization of a Novel Androgen Receptor Coregulator, EAP1 (PMID: 34585037)
summary: EAP1 (IRF2BPL) was identified by rapid immunoprecipitation mass spectrometry as a labile AR interactor. It enhances AR transcriptional activity through E3 ubiquitin ligase activity, with AR and HDAC1 as ubiquitination substrates. Its expression correlates with AR expression and poor prognosis in prostate cancer specimens.

citation: 2020 - Neurodevelopmental disorder caused by a truncating de novo variant of IRF2BPL (PMID: 33278788)
summary: Bioinformatic PPI network analysis links IRF2BPL to IRF2 and 10 other genes and to ubiquitin binding. The truncating variant altered the cellular localization of IRF2BPL and significantly decreased ubiquitinated protein levels, suggesting impaired ubiquitin-proteasome function.

citation: 2024 - IRF2BPL-Related Disorder (NEDAMSS) Is Characterized by Pathology Consistent with DRPLA (PMID: 39224955)
summary: The p.Arg188Ter variant gives variable mRNA levels by cell type, with decreased mRNA in brain, and destabilizes the protein in patient-derived cells. Postmortem brain showed DRPLA-like pathology with polyQ inclusions, suggesting a role for the IRF2BPL polyQ tract.

citation: Association between SET expression and glioblastoma cell apoptosis and proliferation (PMID: 27698810)
sample_size: 32 tissue samples (18 glioma, 2 meningioma, 12 normal brain); U251 and U87MG cell lines
significance: Glioma vs normal brain P=0.001; apoptosis P=0.001 and P<0.001; proliferation P=0.002 and P=0.015; migration P=0.001
summary: siRNA knockdown of SET in U87MG and U251 glioblastoma cells increased apoptosis and reduced proliferation and migration. It also lowered Bcl-2 and raised Bax and caspase-3 mRNA and protein. SET protein is nuclear and higher in glioma tissue than in normal brain, and higher expression tracks with WHO grade.

citation: Up-regulation of I-2(PP2A)/SET gene expression in rat primary hepatomas and regenerating livers (PMID: 11078917)
significance: Reported as significantly elevated (no p-value given)
summary: SET/I-2(PP2A) is expressed ubiquitously across rat tissues but at low levels in liver. Expression is elevated in primary hepatomas and hyperplastic nodules. In regenerating liver it rises 12-24 h after partial hepatectomy, at the mid-G1 to S transition, which links SET to hepatocyte proliferation.

citation: Expression level of SET gene in acute myeloid leukemia and its clinical significance (PMID: 24857208)
significance: OS P=0.001; EFS P=0.005; CR rate P=0.005
summary: High SET transcript level in de novo AML was associated with higher WBC counts, lower complete remission rate, and shorter overall and event-free survival. SET overexpression was an independent prognostic factor for overall survival.

citation: Study on relationship between Set gene expression and clinical manifestations in bone marrow of patients with acute myelogenous leukemia (PMID: 29534404)
significance: CR rate P=0.01; OS P=0.021; EFS P=0.017
summary: SET expression was significantly higher in AML bone marrow than in healthy controls. High expression correlated with marrow blast percentage and lower complete remission rate (32.1% vs 83.9%), and with poor OS and EFS. SET is proposed as an independent poor prognostic marker.

citation: The set gene is a potential oncogene in human colorectal adenocarcinoma and oral squamous cell carcinoma (PMID: 21725597)
sample_size: 30 paired colorectal tumor/normal tissues; Ls174 and HSC3 cell lines
significance: Apoptosis significantly higher than controls (p-value not given in abstract)
summary: SET mRNA was upregulated in 70% of colorectal adenocarcinoma samples compared with matched normal tissue. siRNA knockdown in Ls174 colon and HSC3 oral squamous carcinoma cells reduced proliferation (about 20%) and increased apoptosis (about 18%), consistent with an oncogenic role.

citation: Regulation of SET Gene Expression by NFkB (PMID: 27351675)
summary: The human SET promoter contains a functional NFkB-responsive element, shown by luciferase and EMSA assays. NFkB overexpression or activation upregulates SET isoform 1 but not isoform 2. SET is elevated and mislocalized to the cytoplasm in Alzheimer's disease and Down syndrome brain, where it inhibits PP2A and contributes to tau pathology. The findings link oxidative stress and inflammation to abnormal SET expression.

citation: Cellular localization and expression of template-activating factor I in different cell types (PMID: 9597000)
summary: TAF-I beta is the protein encoded by SET and acts as a chromatin remodeling factor. It is ubiquitously expressed in mouse tissues and conserved from yeast to human. Levels are stable through the cell cycle, and the protein is predominantly nuclear. Loss of the acidic region, which is essential for activity, leads to both nuclear and cytoplasmic localization.

citation: MiR-502-3P suppresses cell proliferation, migration, and invasion in hepatocellular carcinoma by targeting SET (PMID: 27330307)
summary: SET is a direct target of miR-502-3P in HCC. miR-502-3P is downregulated in HCC cell lines and patient samples. Overexpressing it inhibits HCC proliferation, metastasis, invasion and adhesion, which implicates SET in HCC malignant behavior.

citation: SET oncogene is upregulated in pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia (PMID: 22677993)
summary: SET was overexpressed in 96.5% of B-ALL samples (16.6-fold) and 93% of T-ALL samples (47.6-fold) from BCR-ABL-negative pediatric patients. The upregulation was not associated with clinical features or survival.

citation: Identification and characterization of a SET/NAP protein encoded by a brain-specific gene, MB20 (PMID: 11161794)
summary: MB20 is a brain-specific member of the NAP/SET family with a C-terminus homologous to SET proteins. It binds histones and is found in both cytoplasm and nucleus, and the N-terminal region controls its nuclear localization. These properties suggest a role in modulating nucleosome structure and gene expression during brain development.

citation: Robson et al. 2019 - Histone H2B monoubiquitination regulates heart development via epigenetic control of cilia motility (PMID: 31235600)
phenotype: rnf20 knockdown decreased rfx3 mRNA; abnormal heart looping; defective left-right asymmetry; impaired cilia motility; exogenous rfx3 rescues the Rnf20 depletion phenotype

citation: Harris et al. 2021 - Disruption of RFX family transcription factors causes autism, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, intellectual disability, and dysregulated behavior (PMID: 33658631)
sample_size: 38 individuals from 33 unrelated families (RFX3, RFX4, RFX7 combined)
summary: De novo deleterious RFX3, RFX4 and RFX7 variants were found in individuals with ASD, intellectual disability and/or ADHD. RFX3 is strongly expressed in developing and adult human brain, and X-box motifs and RFX ChIP-seq peaks are enriched in the cis-regulatory regions of known ASD risk genes.

citation: Multi-omic analysis of the ciliogenic transcription factor RFX3 reveals a role in promoting activity-dependent responses via enhancing CREB binding in human neurons (PMID: 40060598)
summary: In human iPSC-derived neurons and forebrain organoids, biallelic RFX3 loss disrupted ciliary gene expression and delayed neuronal differentiation. Monoallelic loss disrupted synaptic gene expression and activity-dependent transcription. RFX3 binding sites co-localized with CREB sites, and RFX3 deficiency decreased CREB binding and impaired induction of CREB targets after depolarization.

citation: The transcription factor Rfx3 regulates beta-cell differentiation, function, and glucokinase expression (PMID: 20413507)
summary: Rfx3-/- and pancreas-specific Rfx3 knockout mice showed incompletely differentiated beta-cells with reduced insulin, Glut2 and Gck, and adults were glucose intolerant. Rfx3 knockdown in Min6 cells impaired glucose-stimulated insulin secretion. Rfx3 binds the Pal-1 and Pal-2 elements of the glucokinase neuroendocrine promoter in Min6 cells and human islets.

citation: RFX3 is essential for the generation of functional human pancreatic islets from stem cells (PMID: 40263183)
summary: RFX3 is highly expressed in endocrine populations during iPSC-derived islet differentiation. CRISPR RFX3 KO reduced hormone-positive cells and impaired beta cell function and insulin secretion. KO also increased enterochromaffin cell specification, TXNIP levels and apoptosis, and RFX3 overexpression rescued the dysregulated genes.

citation: A deficiency in RFX3 causes hydrocephalus associated with abnormal differentiation of ependymal cells (PMID: 16930429)
summary: RFX3 is strongly expressed in ciliated ependymal cells of the subcommissural organ, choroid plexus and ventricular walls. Rfx3-deficient mice develop hydrocephalus with choroid plexus differentiation defects, SCO agenesis and reduced SCO-spondin expression from E14.5.

citation: The transcription factor RFX3 directs nodal cilium development and left-right asymmetry specification (PMID: 15121860)
summary: Rfx3 is expressed in ciliated node cells. Rfx3-deficient mice show stunted nodal cilia, left-right asymmetry defects, embryonic lethality and situs inversus. RFX3 regulates expression of D2lic, an intraflagellar transport gene.

citation: RFX3 governs growth and beating efficiency of motile cilia in mouse and controls the expression of genes involved in human ciliopathies (PMID: 19671664)
summary: In primary multiciliated cultures from Rfx3-/- mouse brain, motile cilia growth and beating were impaired. RFX3 is required for optimal FOXJ1 expression and binds directly to axonemal dynein gene promoters.

citation: RFX3 modulation of FOXJ1 regulation of cilia genes in the human airway epithelium (PMID: 23822649)
summary: RFX3 and FOXJ1 interact by immunoprecipitation in human airway basal cells. RFX3 alone did not induce cilia genes, but it acted as a co-activator that enhanced FOXJ1-driven cilia gene promoter activity and mRNA expression.

citation: Auto-fatty acylation of transcription factor RFX3 regulates ciliogenesis (PMID: 30127002)
summary: RFX3 is S-fatty acylated at a conserved cysteine in its dimerization domain, through enzyme-independent auto-acylation with a preference for stearic and oleic acid. A fatty acylation-deficient mutant had reduced homodimerization and failed to promote ciliary gene expression and ciliogenesis, and it impaired Hedgehog signaling.

citation: CircRFX3 Up-regulates Its Host Gene RFX3 to Facilitate Tumorigenesis and Progression of Glioma (PMID: 35416616)
summary: CircRFX3 recruits HNRNPK to stabilize RFX3 mRNA in glioma cells. RFX3 in turn promotes PROX1 transcription, driving glioma cell malignancy and tumor growth.

variant_detail: De novo mutations in CASZ1 (specific variants not given in the abstract); CASZ1 reached family-wise error rate significance for DNM excess (p < 3.64E-07) in 17,426 NDD trios
phenotype: neurodevelopmental disorder; autism spectrum disorder
diagnostic_reason: Significant excess of de novo mutations in CASZ1 in NDD trios (FWER significant), supporting CASZ1 as an NDD risk gene

phenotype: Hypoplasia of myocardium; Ventricular septal defect; Disorganized cardiac morphology / cardiac noncompaction; Decreased cardiomyocyte proliferation; Abnormal expression of muscle contraction genes (Tnni2, Tnnt1, Ckm), Acta1, and ion channel genes (Abcc9, Cacna1d)

citation: Casz1 is required for both inner hair cell fate stabilization and outer hair cell survival (PMID: 39883789)
phenotype: Transdifferentiation of inner hair cells into outer hair cells; OHC production unaffected; Progressive loss of outer hair cells (impaired long-term OHC survival); Gata3 down-regulation in Casz1-deleted IHCs; Hearing impairment, partially rescued by Gata3 overexpression

citation: A single-cell time-series atlas of endothelial cell embryonic development (PMID: 41702400)
phenotype: Impaired vascular growth; Disturbed pulmonary endothelial organotypic differentiation; Deficient epithelial-endothelial crosstalk in lung

citation: CASZ1 promotes vascular assembly and morphogenesis through the direct regulation of an EGFL7/RhoA-mediated pathway (PMID: 23639441)
phenotype: Failure to develop a branched and lumenized vascular system; Defective blood vessel assembly and morphogenesis; Reduced Egfl7 and RhoA expression (in human endothelial cells)

citation: A Casz1-NuRD complex regulates temporal identity transitions in neural progenitors (PMID: 33594190)
phenotype: Altered transition between neurogenesis and gliogenesis in retina; Reduced rod fate and increased gliogenesis upon Casz1 loss

citation: Congenital heart disease protein 5 associates with CASZ1 to maintain myocardial tissue integrity (PMID: 24993940)
phenotype: CASZ1 depletion produced cardiac phenotypes similar to, but milder than, CHD5 depletion; CHD5 loss caused compromised myocardial integrity, improper basement membrane deposition, and failure of cardiac cell movements and tube formation; CHD5-CASZ1 interaction necessary for cardiac morphogenesis

citation: Mouse endothelial atlas study 2026 - A single-cell time-series atlas of endothelial cell embryonic development (PMID: 41702400)
summary: Casz1 was identified as a pulmonary EC-enriched transcription factor in a mouse embryonic endothelial scRNA-seq atlas. Endothelial-specific Casz1 knockout impaired vascular growth, disturbed pulmonary endothelial organotypic differentiation, and weakened epithelial-EC crosstalk.

citation: CASZ1 upregulates PI3K-AKT-mTOR signaling and promotes T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (PMID: 38058200)
summary: TAL1 directly and positively regulates CASZ1. T-ALL samples overexpress the CASZ1b isoform, and its expression correlates with PI3K-AKT-mTOR activation. CASZ1b overexpression activates PI3K signaling, which is required for transformation of Ba/F3 cells. CASZ1b cooperates with activated NOTCH1 in zebrafish T-ALL and confers chemoresistance.

citation: A Casz1-NuRD complex regulates temporal identity transitions in neural progenitors (PMID: 33594190)
summary: BioID proteomics showed Casz1 interacts with the NuRD complex in retinal cells. Casz1 controls the neurogenesis-to-gliogenesis transition. NuRD and polycomb are both required for Casz1 to promote rod fate and suppress gliogenesis.

citation: CASZ1 loss-of-function mutation contributes to familial dilated cardiomyopathy (PMID: 28099117)
significance: Absent in 400 control chromosomes; co-segregation with disease
summary: A heterozygous nonsense CASZ1 variant, p.K351X, was found in a DCM family and co-segregated with disease in an autosomal dominant pattern with complete penetrance. The mutant protein had no transcriptional activity in luciferase reporter assays.

citation: CASZ1 regulates the maturation of outer hair cells and is required for hearing in mice (PMID: 42707066)
summary: Casz1 is an ATOH1 target gene. Its deletion during cochlear development caused hearing loss, disorganized OHC stereocilia, reduced cuticular plate F-actin, and progressive OHC loss. Casz1 loss delayed downregulation of immature OHC genes such as Coro2a, and deleting Coro2a partially rescued F-actin density.

citation: Loss of CASZ1 tumor suppressor linked to oncogenic subversion of neuroblastoma core regulatory circuitry (PMID: 36243768)
summary: CASZ1 is highly expressed in developing chromaffin cells but silenced in neuroblastoma cells. HAND2 directly represses CASZ1. Restoring CASZ1 upregulates noradrenergic neuronal genes and represses core regulatory circuit components by remodeling enhancers, inducing differentiation.

citation: CASZ1 induces skeletal muscle and rhabdomyosarcoma differentiation through a feed-forward loop with MYOD and MYOG (PMID: 32060262)
summary: CASZ1 upregulates MYOD signature genes and drives skeletal muscle differentiation in myoblasts and ERMS cells. RAS-MEK signaling suppresses CASZ1 expression. ChIP-seq, ATAC-seq and RNA-seq show CASZ1 directly activates muscle genes and represses non-muscle genes by altering chromatin accessibility and super-enhancers. A CASZ1 coding SNV was found in a primary RMS tumor.

citation: Casz1 controls higher-order nuclear organization in rod photoreceptors (PMID: 30072429)
summary: Conditional Casz1 deletion disrupts the inverted chromatin organization of rods and their survival. Casz1 interacts with polycomb repressor complex in a splice variant-specific manner, and both suppress lamin A/C expression. Casz1 is sufficient to expand and centralize heterochromatin in fibroblasts.

citation: CASZ1 promotes migration, invasion, and metastasis of lung cancer cells by controlling expression of ITGAV (PMID: 36777515)
summary: CASZ1 expression in lung cancer is positively associated with metastasis and poor prognosis. CASZ1b overexpression promotes migration, invasion and EMT, while knockdown suppresses them and reduces metastasis in vivo. CASZ1 binds the ITGAV promoter and transcriptionally regulates ITGAV.

citation: CASZ1b is a novel transcriptional corepressor of mineralocorticoid receptor (PMID: 33077905)
summary: CASZ1b was identified by mass spectrometry as an MR-interacting factor, interacting in an aldosterone-dependent manner and colocalizing with MR in kidney. It recruits the Mi-2/NuRD complex to suppress ENaCα and SGK1. Overexpression reduced MR activity by about 50%, and knockdown raised ENaCα and SGK1 expression about 2-fold and 2.3-fold.

summary: By immunohistochemistry, nuclear SOX11 is highly expressed in SCLC (63.33% positive) but low or absent in carcinoid/neuroendocrine tumors (12.5%), lung adenocarcinoma (0%) and squamous cell carcinoma (0%). SOX11 showed sensitivity 0.633 and specificity 0.875 as an SCLC diagnostic marker.

citation: Regulation of SOX11 expression through CCND1 and STAT3 in mantle cell lymphoma (PMID: 30530749)
summary: CCND1 interacts with and sequesters HDAC1/2 from the SOX11 locus, increasing H3K9/14 acetylation and SOX11 transcription. Phospho-Y705 STAT3 is inversely related to SOX11: JAK/STAT3 inhibition raises SOX11, while IL-21-induced or constitutively active STAT3 lowers it. SOX11 knockdown is toxic to SOX11+ MCL cells.

citation: SOX11 regulates apoptosis and cell cycle in hepatocellular carcinoma via Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway (PMID: 30517979)
summary: SOX11 is decreased in HCC tumors versus matched normal tissue. Overexpression in HuH-7 cells inhibits growth and induces apoptosis. It increases nemo-like kinase expression and TCF4 phosphorylation, which suppresses Wnt/β-catenin signaling, and it sensitizes cells to cisplatin and 5-FU, suggesting a tumor suppressor role.

citation: SOX11 as a potential prognostic biomarker in hepatocellular carcinoma linked to immune infiltration and ferroptosis (PMID: 39246708)
summary: In contrast to the earlier HCC report, SOX11 was elevated in HCC (TCGA/GEO, validated by IHC) and predicted survival. It correlated with immune infiltration, immune checkpoint genes and ferroptosis genes. SOX11 knockdown in HepG2 and HuH7 cells reduced proliferation and migration.

citation: SOX11 promotes epithelial/mesenchymal hybrid state and alters tropism of invasive breast cancer cells (PMID: 32909943)
summary: SOX11 is an embryonic mammary epithelial marker normally silenced before birth. In ER-negative DCIS.com cells, SOX11 drives hybrid epithelial/mesenchymal, invasive populations. In xenografts, SOX11-high cells metastasize more to brain and bone and less to lung.

citation: Human fetal cerebellar cell atlas informs medulloblastoma origin and oncogenesis (PMID: 36450980)
summary: SOX11 was identified, together with HNRNPH1, as a transcriptional determinant in transitional cerebellar progenitors enriched in group 3 medulloblastoma, and it correlates with prognosis. SOX11-targeted super-enhancers form long-range chromatin loops to MYC cis-regulatory elements. Targeting these regulators inhibited MYC expression and group 3 MB growth.

citation: SOX11 regulates PAX5 expression and blocks terminal B-cell differentiation in aggressive mantle cell lymphoma (PMID: 23321250)
summary: SOX11 promotes tumor growth in an MCL xenograft model. ChIP-on-chip with expression profiling after knockdown identified PAX5 as a major direct target. SOX11 silencing downregulates PAX5, induces BLIMP1 and shifts cells toward plasmacytic differentiation, so SOX11 blocks terminal B-cell differentiation.

citation: Sox11 is an Activity-Regulated Gene with Dentate-Gyrus-Specific Expression Upon General Neural Activation (PMID: 32080705)
summary: In adult mice, SOX11 is induced within 6 h by electroconvulsive stimulation or novel environment exploration, restricted to dentate gyrus granule neurons; ~75% of SOX11+ DG neurons are c-FOS+. SOX11 overexpression enhanced granule cell excitability and downregulated potassium channel subunits, whereas conditional Sox11/4 knockout showed the opposite phenotype.

citation: Lineage specific transcription factor waves reprogram neuroblastoma from self-renewal to differentiation (PMID: 38653778)
summary: The SOX11 super-enhancer and SOX11 expression decrease with ATRA-induced neuroblastoma differentiation. CRISPR-Cas9 and siRNA show neuroblastoma cells depend on SOX11 in vitro and in vivo. dCAS9-KRAB silencing of the SOX11 SE reduces SOX11 mRNA and inhibits growth.

citation: ASHG 2016 - SOX11 is necessary for development of the bony labyrinth (Sperry et al.)
sample_size: Sox11+/- n=26 ears (10 abnormal); Sox11-/- n=12 ears
summary: Sox11-/- mice show lateral semicircular canal fusion plate failure and canal dysplasia, and Sox11+/- mice show canal abnormalities and mild high-frequency hearing loss. Bmp4, Otx1 and Shh are misregulated. Sox11 expression depends on CHD7 in a dosage-dependent manner (reduced in Chd7 Gt/+, absent in Gt/Gt ears), linking SOX11 to Coffin-Siris and CHARGE pathogenesis.

knockout_type: other (Ski-deficient mice, with Satb2 as partner; Satb2 requirement shown for Ctip2 repression)

phenotype: Adult colonic mucosa lacking SATB2 converts to small intestine; Activation of lipid absorptive genes; Functional lipid uptake after MTA2 loss; HNF4A released from colonic chromatin and accumulating on small intestinal chromatin; SATB2 restrains colonic plasticity through an HNF4A-dependent mechanism

phenotype: Single-cell genotypes of CRISPR-targeted neurons matched Satb2 protein loss and phenotypes
knockout_type: knockdown (CRISPR/Cas9 in utero electroporation, focal knockout)

citation: Semaphorin heterodimerization in cis regulates membrane targeting and neocortical wiring (PMID: 39152101)
summary: In murine neocortex, Satb2 controls neuronal migration and callosal axon outgrowth by inducing expression of the GPI-anchored Sema7A. Sema7A heterodimerizes in cis with Sema4D and promotes Sema4D plasma membrane targeting. This places Satb2 upstream of a Sema7A/Sema4D semaphorin pathway relevant to SATB2-associated syndrome.

citation: SATB2 preserves colon stem cell identity and mediates ileum-colon conversion via enhancer remodeling (PMID: 34582804)
summary: SATB2 is a colon-restricted chromatin factor that preserves LGR5+ colonic stem cell identity in mice and humans. Satb2 loss converts colonic stem cells into ileal-like stem cells, and SATB2 modulates enhancer binding of CDX2 and HNF4A. Human colonic organoids acquire ileal characteristics when SATB2 is lost.

citation: Protein translation rate determines neocortical neuron fate (PMID: 38849354)
summary: A small-molecule screen identified Ire1α as a regulator of Satb2 expression and neuronal polarity. Satb2 mRNA translation requires eIF4A1 helicase activity acting on its 5'-UTR. Satb2 expression in cortical neurons is therefore controlled post-transcriptionally by translation.

citation: Satb2 is required for the regionalization of retrosplenial cortex (PMID: 31666685)
summary: In Satb2 conditional knockout mice, the Rsp/subiculum boundary is lost, Rsp-specific genes are lost, and subiculum genes are ectopically expressed. Satb2 acts as a transcriptional repressor of Nr4a2 and Ctip2, and this repression specifies retrosplenial identity cell-autonomously.

citation: The expression profile and function of Satb2 in zebrafish embryonic development (PMID: 20814748)
summary: Zebrafish satb2 is ubiquitously expressed from the 1-cell to the 10-somite stage, then becomes restricted to the pronephric duct (24 hpf), branchial arches (36 hpf), and retinal ganglion cell layer and fins (48 hpf). Knockdown arrests embryos at 50-60% epiboly, impairs cell migration, and reduces dynamin II and VAMP4. Knockdown also disorganizes actin and the yolk syncytial layer.

citation: SATB2 drives glioblastoma growth by recruiting CBP to promote FOXM1 expression in glioma stem cells (PMID: 33124191)
summary: SATB2 is preferentially expressed in glioma stem cells. It binds the MAR of the FOXM1 locus and recruits the histone acetyltransferase CBP to activate FOXM1 and drive proliferation. SATB2 knockdown reduces GSC proliferation and GBM growth, and the CBP inhibitor C646 suppresses growth in vitro and in vivo.

citation: Satb1 and Satb2 regulate embryonic stem cell differentiation and Nanog expression (PMID: 19933152)
summary: Satb2 is upregulated in Satb1-/- ES cells. Forced Satb2 expression in wild-type ES cells antagonizes differentiation-associated silencing of Nanog, and both Satb1 and Satb2 bind the Nanog locus in vivo. Satb1 and Satb2 thus act antagonistically on Nanog expression and pluripotency.

citation: SATB2 expression increased anchorage-independent growth and cell migration in human bronchial epithelial cells (PMID: 26780400)
summary: Ectopic SATB2 expression in BEAS-2B cells increased anchorage-independent growth and migration. shRNA knockdown reduced growth in Ni-transformed cells. RNA-seq showed SATB2-regulated genes enriched in cytoskeleton, cell adhesion and cell movement pathways. SATB2 expression is also induced in cells transformed by As, Cr, Ni and V.

citation: miR-29a-5p Targets SATB2 and Regulates the SIRT1/Smad3 Deacetylation Pathway to Inhibit Thoracic Ligamentum Flavum Cell Osteogenesis (PMID: 32205703)
summary: SATB2 is upregulated in ossified thoracic ligamentum flavum tissue, and miR-29a-5p directly targets and suppresses it (dual luciferase assay). SATB2 knockdown reduced SIRT1 expression and Smad3 acetylation and blunted the miR-29a-5p effect on osteogenesis, placing SATB2 upstream of the SIRT1/Smad3 pathway.

citation: Multiomic profiling of transcription factor binding and function in human brain (PMID: 38831039); ASHG 2023 - Extensive profiling of transcription factors in postmortem brains
summary: ChIP-seq in human postmortem brain shows that the neuronal TFs SATB2 and TBR1 bind unique regions depleted of high-occupancy sites. These regions regulate and promote neuron-specific gene expression, consistent with SATB2 acting as a neuronal transcriptional regulator.

phenotype: Syncrip knockout in radial glial cells disrupts neuronal differentiation; Abnormal neuronal localization; Superficial cortical layer defects; Learning and memory impairments; Late-stage neurogenesis disrupted; transcriptional progression of RGCs stalled (scRNA-seq); Notch signaling pathway dysregulated

citation: RNA binding protein SYNCRIP maintains proteostasis and self-renewal of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (PMID: 37085479)
phenotype: Defects in HSCs and progenitors, especially after regenerative stress; Impaired long-term repopulation after secondary transplantation; Increased protein synthesis; Dysregulated epichaperome and accumulation of misfolded proteins; ER stress; Reduced CDC42 translation with defects in polarity and asymmetric segregation; Rescue of polarity and replating by forced CDC42 expression

citation: Functional screen of MSI2 interactors identifies an essential role for SYNCRIP in myeloid leukemia stem cells (PMID: 28436985)
phenotype: shRNA depletion of Syncrip delayed leukemogenesis in vivo; Increased apoptosis and differentiation of leukemia cells; Loss of MLL and HOXA9 leukemia stem cell program; Reduced HOXA9 translation; Syncrip was the most differentially required gene between normal and myeloid leukemia cells

citation: Deletion 6q Drives T-cell Leukemia Progression by Ribosome Modulation (PMID: 30266814)
phenotype: Combined silencing of Syncrip and Snhg5, but not either alone, accelerated leukemogenesis in a Tal1/Lmo1/Notch1-driven mouse model; Decreased ribosome and mitochondrial activities; Increased leukemia-initiating cell activity in xenografts of primary human leukemic cells upon co-silencing

citation: Zhang et al. 2023 - RNA binding protein SYNCRIP maintains proteostasis and self-renewal of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (PMID: 37085479)
summary: In a conditional knockout mouse, SYNCRIP loss impaired HSC maintenance, especially after regenerative stress. Loss increased protein synthesis, dysregulated the epichaperome, caused misfolded protein accumulation and ER stress. SYNCRIP is required for CDC42 translation, and forced CDC42 expression rescued HSC polarity and replating activity.

citation: Zhang et al. 2025 - Posttranscriptional Control of Neural Progenitors Temporal Dynamics During Neocortical Development by Syncrip (PMID: 39776340)
summary: Syncrip knockout in radial glial cells caused superficial cortical layer defects and learning and memory impairment in mice. scRNA-seq showed stalled late-stage neurogenesis. Syncrip stabilizes temporal transcription factor mRNAs via phase-separated complexes and regulates Notch signaling. Pathogenic human variants weaken its phase separation.

citation: Loss of SYNCRIP unleashes APOBEC-driven mutagenesis, tumor heterogeneity, and AR-targeted therapy resistance in prostate cancer (PMID: 37478850)
summary: In prostate cancer cells, SYNCRIP acts as a brake on APOBEC3B-driven mutagenesis. SYNCRIP deficiency activates APOBEC3B, which mutates drivers such as FOXA1, EP300 and AR and promotes resistance to AR-targeted therapy. A functional screen identified eight APOBEC3B-mutated resistance drivers.

citation: RNA-binding protein syncrip regulates starvation-induced hyperactivity in adult Drosophila (PMID: 33617535)
summary: A GWAS in the DGRP (Drosophila Genetic Reference Panel) with RNAi validation identified syp as a starvation-induced hyperactivity gene. Neuron-specific syp knockdown decreased SIH, while ubiquitous knockdown caused semi-lethality. syp is alternatively spliced under starvation without a change in expression level, and an alternative-exon-specific KO reduced SIH.

citation: Syncrip/hnRNP Q influences synaptic transmission and regulates BMP signaling at the Drosophila neuromuscular synapse (PMID: 25171887)
summary: Syncrip is detected in muscle but not in the motoneuron at the Drosophila NMJ. It is required for normal vesicle release and synapse structure. It modulates retrograde BMP signaling by influencing levels of the BMP ligand Glass bottom boat.

citation: SYNCRIP, a new player in pri-let-7a processing (PMID: 31907208)
summary: SYNCRIP binds pri-let-7a, mainly through its terminal loop, and associates with the microprocessor complex. It promotes pri-let-7a processing through its RRM2-3 domain. Knockdown reduces let-7a and overexpression increases it, and SYNCRIP silencing changes a broader set of miRNAs.

citation: The cytoplasmic SYNCRIP mRNA interactome of mammalian neurons (PMID: 33030396)
summary: iCLIP in primary rat cortical neurons identified hundreds of SYNCRIP target mRNAs, enriched for neurogenesis, migration and neurite outgrowth genes. These include microtubule-related mRNAs such as Dcx, which SYNCRIP stabilizes. SYNCRIP synergizes with miR-9 and neuronal miRISC to promote early neuronal differentiation.

citation: SYNCRIP (hnRNP Q1/NSAP1) is a component of mRNA granule transported with IP3R1 mRNA in neuronal dendrites (PMID: 15475564)
summary: SYNCRIP is mainly in the cell bodies of rat hippocampal neurons, with punctate expression in proximal dendrites. GFP-SYNCRIP granules move bidirectionally in a microtubule-dependent manner (nocodazole-sensitive). They co-transport with Staufen1 and the IP3R1 3'UTR, and overlap with dendritic RNA and EF1α.

citation: SYNCRIP, a cytoplasmic counterpart of hnRNP R, interacts with ubiquitous synaptotagmin isoforms (PMID: 10734137)
summary: SYNCRIP binds the C2B domains of Syt-VII, -VIII and -IX, shown by in vitro binding and co-IP in COS cells. It binds RNA with a preference for poly(A). It is ubiquitously expressed across mouse tissues and is predominantly cytoplasmic, unlike nuclear hnRNP R.

citation: SYNCRIP is a host factor involved in hepatitis C virus RNA replication (PMID: 19232660)
summary: SYNCRIP associates with detergent-resistant membrane fractions and colocalizes with newly synthesized HCV RNA. siRNA knockdown reduced HCV RNA in replicon and full-length RNA systems. Immunodepletion in an in vitro replication assay showed SYNCRIP is directly involved in HCV RNA replication.

citation: Lymphocyte-Specific Function of the DNA Polymerase Epsilon Subunit Pole3 Revealed by Neomorphic Alleles (PMID: 32553171)
summary: Pole3-null mice survive to late embryonic stages, so Pole3 is dispensable for DNA replication. Hypomorphic and neomorphic alleles show a stage-specific role for the Pole3 histone fold domain in T and B cell development. Adding positive charges to the acidic C terminus causes peripheral lymphopenia of increasing severity, pointing to non-replicative, cell-type-specific functions.

citation: The genetic and biochemical basis of human leading strand synthesis (PMID: 41339636)
summary: CRISPR screens in POLE4-null cells, together with biochemistry and structural modelling, identified a synthetic lethal interaction between POLE3-POLE4 and CHTF18-RFC2/5. POLE3-POLE4 "grips" newly synthesised dsDNA to support Polε processivity, in parallel with CHTF18-RFC2/5-dependent PCNA loading. Losing both is incompatible with leading strand synthesis and viability.

citation: The Pole3 bidirectional unit is regulated by MYC and E2Fs (PMID: 16403426)
summary: Pole3 expression in serum-stimulated NIH3T3 cells peaks at S-phase entry. Its bidirectional promoter, shared with C9orf46, has an E box and E2F sites. ChIP showed phase-specific binding of E2F1/4 and MYC to the promoter, so Pole3 is co-regulated with core histones during DNA synthesis.

citation: Asymmetric distribution of parental H3K9me3 in S phase silences L1 elements (PMID: 37938774)
summary: The HUSH complex interacts with Pol ε to promote asymmetric transfer of parental H3K9me3 to leading strands at head-on LINE-1 elements. Cells deficient in POLE3 or POLE4 lose H3K9me3 asymmetry and show increased LINE expression.

citation: Requirement of WDR70 for POLE3-mediated DNA double-strand breaks repair (PMID: 37682991)
summary: POLE3 interacts with CHRAC1 to promote DNA repair, by regulating homology-directed repair proteins and KU80 recruitment. A colorectal cancer CHRAC1 D121Y mutation weakens the POLE3 interaction and impairs repair. H2BK120ub1 and H3K79me2 at the POLE3 locus depend on WDR70 and on POLE3 transcription.

citation: Stable inheritance of H3.3-containing nucleosomes during mitotic cell divisions (PMID: 35523900)
summary: The Pole3-Pole4 pathway, alongside Mcm2-Pola1, takes part in transferring parental H3.1 and H3.3 histones after DNA replication. Pole3 and Pole4 mutants defective in parental histone transfer show chromosome segregation defects.

citation: A consensus set of genetic vulnerabilities to ATR inhibition (PMID: 31506018)
summary: Genome-scale CRISPR/Cas9 screens found that loss of the Polε accessory subunits POLE3 and POLE4 causes marked hypersensitivity to ATR inhibitors.

citation: MMS22L-TONSL functions in sister chromatid cohesion in a pathway parallel to DSCC1-RFC (PMID: 36622344)
summary: A genome-wide CRISPR screen in DSCC1-KO cells showed that they require POLE3 for survival. Co-depleting DSCC1 and POLE3 additively impairs DNA replication, so the two factors support leading-strand replication in parallel.

citation: Orthoxenografts of Testicular Germ Cell Tumors Demonstrate Genomic Changes Associated with Cisplatin Resistance and Identify PDMP as a Resensitizing Agent (PMID: 29618620)
summary: POLE3 and AKNA were the only two genes in the 9q32-q33.1 region deregulated in cisplatin-resistant testicular germ cell tumors carrying the 9q32-q33.1 gain. This links POLE3 expression to acquired cisplatin resistance.

citation: USP15 Promotes Pancreatic Cancer Progression and Cisplatin Resistance By Activating DNA Damage Repair (PMID: 41950365)
summary: USP15 binds POLE3 (confirmed by Co-IP) and suppresses its ubiquitination-dependent degradation. This stabilizes POLE3, promotes DNA damage repair and drives cisplatin resistance in pancreatic cancer cells.

citation: De novo variants in CELF2 that disrupt the nuclear localization signal cause developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (PMID: 33131106)

citation: Unknown et al. - The RNA-Binding Protein CELF2 Inhibits Ovarian Cancer Progression by Stabilizing FAM198B (PMID: 33335801)
summary: CELF2 binds AU/U-rich elements in the 3' UTR of FAM198B and increases its mRNA stability (post-transcriptional regulation). The CELF2/FAM198B axis represses ovarian cancer proliferation, migration and invasion, likely via inhibiting MAPK/ERK signaling. CELF2 is downregulated in ovarian cancer, and curcumin-induced CELF2 increased cisplatin sensitivity.

citation: Unknown et al. - N6-methyladenosine-mediated CELF2 regulates CD44 alternative splicing affecting tumorigenesis via ERAD pathway in pancreatic cancer (PMID: 35941702)

CELF2 regulates CD44 alternative splicing (CD44s to CD44v switch), altering ER stress and the ERAD pathway, thereby affecting apoptosis and stemness; the ERAD inhibitor EerI reverses the CD44 effects.

citation: Unknown et al. - Epigenetic inactivation of the splicing RNA-binding protein CELF2 in human breast cancer (PMID: 31409895)

citation: Unknown et al. - CELF2 regulates the species-specific alternative splicing of TREM2 (PMID: 33093587)
summary: CELF2 and CELF1 overexpression promotes TREM2 exon 3 skipping, with a CELF-responsive element mapped to intron 3 of human TREM2 using chimeric minigenes. Only CELF2 reduced full-length TREM2 protein. The regulation is conserved in human and monkey but not mouse, and links CELF2 to Alzheimer's disease-relevant TREM2 regulation.

citation: Unknown et al. - Activation of MAP3K DLK and LZK in Purkinje cells causes rapid and slow degeneration depending on signaling strength (PMID: 33475086)

citation: Unknown et al. - LncRNA Dleu2 regulates fear extinction memory through Celf2-driven synaptic plasticity (PMID: 41628728)

citation: Unknown et al. - Diversity and conservation of CELF1 and CELF2 RNA and protein expression patterns during embryonic development (PMID: 23468433)
summary: CELF2 is broadly expressed in developing tissues, with protein levels regulated independently of transcript levels in the heart. It shows nuclear and cytoplasmic and tissue-specific isoforms, and is co-expressed with CELF1 but in mutually exclusive territories in some organs (heart, eye). Patterns are conserved between chicken and mouse.

citation: Unknown et al. - Reduced Expression of RNA Binding Protein CELF2, a Putative Tumor Suppressor Gene in Colon Cancer (PMID: 23795348)

summary: Immunohistochemistry shows CELF2 is reduced in colon tumors compared with normal colon. It is predominantly nuclear in normal cells but shows diffuse cytoplasmic staining in cancer tissue. This supports a tumor suppressor role.

citation: Conserved pharmacological rescue of hereditary spastic paraplegia-related phenotypes across model organisms (PMID: 26744324)
summary: Null SPAST homologues in C. elegans, Drosophila and zebrafish show locomotor defects linked to ER stress. These defects were partially rescued by phenazine, methylene blue, N-acetyl-cysteine, guanabenz and salubrinal, and ER stress biomarkers correlated with the improvement.

citation: Spastin binds to lipid droplets and affects lipid metabolism (PMID: 25875445)
summary: Spastin-M1 sorts from the ER to lipid droplets via a hydrophobic motif (aa 57-86, with R65 required). It acts as a conserved positive regulator of lipid droplet metabolism. Dspastin overexpression or knockdown in Drosophila, and spas-1 depletion in C. elegans, altered lipid droplet number and size, triacylglycerol levels and fat stores.

citation: Hereditary spastic paraplegia: gain-of-function mechanisms revealed by new transgenic mouse (PMID: 30520996)
summary: SPAST-C448Y transgenic mice expressing human mutant spastin show adult-onset gait defects and dying-back of corticospinal axons without haploinsufficiency. The mutant alters microtubule stability opposite to haploinsufficiency predictions. Cultured neurons show organelle transport deficits that are worsened by depletion of endogenous spastin, supporting a gain-of-function mechanism.

citation: Modeling gain-of-function and loss-of-function components of SPAST-based hereditary spastic paraplegia using transgenic mice (PMID: 34935948)
summary: Crossing Spast-KO mice with hSPAST-C448Y mice produced axonal swellings, earlier onset, worse gait deficits and more corticospinal dieback than C448Y alone. Changes in HDAC6 and tubulin modifications were also seen in the axon. Loss of function exacerbates mutant toxicity.

citation: Spastin MIT Domain Disease-Associated Mutations Disrupt Lysosomal Function (PMID: 31787869)
summary: Three disease-associated MIT-domain spastin mutants failed to promote endosomal tubule fission, lysosomal enzyme receptor trafficking or normal lysosomal morphology. One mutant impaired recruitment to endosomes, which depends on MIT binding to ESCRT-III proteins. The others did not, suggesting non-canonical MIT roles. Microtubule-severing capacity was unaffected.

citation: Missense mutation of SPAST protein (I344K) results in loss of ATPase activity and prolonged the half-life (PMID: 30006150)
summary: I344K-SPAST has defective ATPase and microtubule-severing activity but a prolonged protein half-life through altered post-translational modification for proteasomal degradation. It causes microtubule accumulation and inhibits neurite growth in neuroblastoma, neural progenitor cells and mouse cortical neurons. Wild-type M1 SPAST interacts with the mutant and reduces these effects dose-dependently.

citation: Alu-mediated SPAST deletion impairs golgi zinc transport and reveals a druggable vulnerability (PMID: 42521669)
summary: An Alu-mediated SPAST exon 17 deletion in hPSC-derived cortical organoids and xenografts creates SPAST-SLC30A6 fusion transcripts and reduces ZnT6 expression. This causes cytosolic zinc accumulation, Golgi fragmentation and Aβ/ubiquitin aggregation. TPEN or a GRASP55-blocking antibody rescued Golgi integrity and reduced Aβ.

citation: CRISPR activation to characterize splice-altering variants in easily accessible cells (PMID: 38272032)
summary: SPAST is predominantly expressed in the CNS and is not readily expressed in skin fibroblasts. dCas9-VPR CRISPRa strongly upregulated SPAST transcription in fibroblasts, enabling profiling of splice-altering variants by RT-PCR, NGS and long-read sequencing.

citation: A novel truncated variant in SPAST results in spastin accumulation and defects in microtubule dynamics (PMID: 38066582)

This suggests toxic accumulation rather than pure haploinsufficiency in a five-generation family.

citation: Møller et al. 2017 - Mutations in GABRB3: From febrile seizures to epileptic encephalopathies (PMID: 28053010)

citation: Orefice et al. 2016 - Peripheral Mechanosensory Neuron Dysfunction Underlies Tactile and Behavioral Deficits in Mouse Models of ASDs (PMID: 27293187)
summary: Gabrb3 mutant mice show altered tactile discrimination and hypersensitivity to gentle touch. Deleting Gabrb3 in peripheral somatosensory neurons removes GABAA receptor-mediated presynaptic inhibition. Deletion during development, but not in adulthood, produced social interaction deficits and anxiety-like behavior.

citation: Understanding paralogous epilepsy-associated GABA(A) receptor variants: Clinical implications, mechanisms, and potential pitfalls (PMID: 39642202)

citation: Gabrb3 is required for the functional integration of pyramidal neuron subtypes in the somatosensory cortex (PMID: 36446382)
summary: Gabrb3 is enriched in contralaterally projecting pyramidal neurons. Its ablation reduces GABAergic synapses, increases local network synchrony, and enhances contralateral functional connectivity and the response to tactile stimulation. In human ASD datasets, the spatial distribution of GABRB3 expression correlates with atypical connectivity.

citation: Gabrb3 endothelial cell-specific knockout mice display abnormal blood flow, hypertension, and behavioral dysfunction (PMID: 35318369)
summary: Endothelial-specific deletion of Gabrb3 reduces vessel density in brain and heart and increases cortical red blood cell velocity and blood flow. It also causes hypertension, abnormal cardiac histology, and behavioral deficits including altered prepulse inhibition and reduced short-term memory. This indicates a role for endothelial GABAA receptor β3 signaling in vascular and cardiac function.

citation: Meta-analysis of GABRB3 Gene Polymorphisms and Susceptibility to Autism Spectrum Disorder (PMID: 30074174)

citation: Genetic analysis of GABRB3 as a candidate gene of autism spectrum disorders (PMID: 24999380)

summary: Rare GABRB3 variants, especially at the 5' regulatory region, were enriched in ASD patients. Reporter gene assays showed that four 5' regulatory variants and one exon 1a UTR variant raised reporter activity, suggesting increased GABRB3 expression may contribute to ASD in some patients.

citation: Structure and organization of GABRB3 and GABRA5 (PMID: 9126483)
summary: GABRB3 spans about 250 kb and has 9 exons. It lies in the 15q11-q13 Prader-Willi/Angelman imprinted region in a cluster with GABRA5 and GABRG3.

citation: ASHG 2017 - Multi-system contributions to Gabrb3-related neurodevelopmental risk in utero

citation: The gain of function SCN1A disorder spectrum: novel epilepsy phenotypes and therapeutic implications (PMID: 35696452)
summary: Whole-cell voltage-clamp of NaV1.1 variants showed gating changes consistent with gain of function and hyperexcitability. Epilepsy variants gave a mild gain of function. Familial hemiplegic migraine type 3 variants gave a stronger one, with increased persistent current and larger action current amplitude. The variants cluster in inactivation regions, unlike Dravet variants. Sodium channel blockers reduced seizures in 81% of gain-of-function patients.

citation: SCN1A gain of function in early infantile encephalopathy (PMID: 30779207)

Dynamic action potential clamp and computational models showed a left-shifted rheobase and greater susceptibility to depolarization block. This is a 'functional dominant negative' effect that explains the severe phenotype.

citation: Biological concepts in human sodium channel epilepsies and their relevance in clinical practice (PMID: 32090326)
summary: SCN1A, SCN2A, SCN3A and SCN8A show significant constraint for both truncating and missense variation. Age at seizure onset relates to temporal SCN gene expression. The functional effects of variants at corresponding channel positions are similar across SCN subtypes, but the clinical outcome differs with the neuron types in which each channel is expressed.

citation: Developmental progression of respiratory dysfunction in a mouse model of Dravet syndrome (PMID: 40924494)
summary: Scn1a+/- mice had a blunted ventilatory response to CO2/H+ before seizures began, and this worsened over time. Pharmacological activation of Nav1.1 rescued activity deficits in retrotrapezoid nucleus neurons, implicating Nav1.1 in inhibitory control of RTN neurons.

citation: Medial septum parvalbumin-expressing inhibitory neurons are impaired in a mouse model of Dravet syndrome (PMID: 40622667)

citation: ASHG 2022 - Long-read sequencing and profiling of RNA-binding proteins reveals the pathogenic mechanism of aberrant splicing of an SCN1A poison exon in individuals with epilepsy
sample_size: 5 variants in 5 individuals; 3 patient iPSC lines
summary: Variants near the SCN1A intron 20 poison exon (20N) increased its inclusion and reduced Nav1.1 protein in patient iPSC-derived neurons. RNA-antisense purification with mass spectrometry in a splicing reporter in HEK293T cells identified differential binding of SRSF1, SRSF3 and HNRNPR to the variant constructs. RNA immunoprecipitation with ddPCR validated these interactions, indicating these RBPs regulate poison exon splicing.

citation: Ste20-Like Kinase TAOK1 Positively Regulates Antiviral Responses by Controlling the TBK1-IRF3 Signaling Axis (PMID: 36649698)

On viral infection TAOK1 switches from MAP4 to dynein, trafficking TBK1 along microtubules to bind IRF3. Virus infection downregulates TAOK1, and TAOK1 deficiency reduces type I IFN production and increases susceptibility to infection.

citation: Oxaloacetate sensing promotes innate immune antiviral defence against influenza virus infection (PMID: 40983701)
summary: TAOK1 phosphorylates the transcription factor ETS2 at serine 313 after ETS2 is recruited by an OAA-sensing MDH1 dimer scaffold. Phosphorylated ETS2 enters the nucleus and supports TBK1 expression and type I interferon responses against influenza.

citation: TAOK1 promotes filament formation in HR repair through phosphorylating USP7 (PMID: 40106350)

TAOK1 phosphorylates USP7, enhancing its activity and protecting RAD51 from ubiquitylation and degradation, which supports HR repair. TAOK1 depletion or inhibition causes RAD51 loss, impaired HR and PARPi sensitivity in cancer cells.

citation: Thousand and one amino acid protein kinase 1 suppression improves doxorubicin-induced cardiomyopathy by preventing cardiomyocyte death and dysfunction (PMID: 39964965)

TAOK1 knockout or knockdown reduced DNA damage, mitochondrial dysfunction and p38 MAPK activation, while overexpression worsened death. AAV-mediated TAOK1 silencing protected the heart in a mouse model of doxorubicin cardiomyopathy.

citation: Silencing of STE20-type kinase TAOK1 confers protection against hepatocellular lipotoxicity through metabolic rewiring (PMID: 36930872)

citation: Targeting TAOK1 with resveratrol inhibits esophageal squamous cell carcinoma growth in vitro and in vivo (PMID: 38376345)

citation: Piazza et al. 2018 - SETBP1 induces transcription of a network of development genes by acting as an epigenetic hub (PMID: 29875417)
summary: SETBP1 binds genomic DNA at AT-rich promoter regions through its AT-hooks and activates transcription by recruiting a HCF1/KMT2A/PHF8 epigenetic complex. citation: Makishima/Sakaguchi et al. 2013 - Somatic SETBP1 mutations in myeloid malignancies (PMID: 23832012)

Mutant Setbp1 immortalized mouse myeloid progenitors with greater proliferative capacity than wild-type Setbp1. Mutations were associated with monosomy 7/del(7q) and poor prognosis.

citation: ASHG 2016 - Genetic and functional comparison of identical germline and somatic SETBP1 mutations
summary: Overexpression experiments show that hotspot mutations destroy the SETBP1 degron and increase protein levels, with varying effects on stability. Saturation genome editing of the hotspot and surrounding region showed that mutations common in leukemia disrupt the degron more strongly than those common in SGS. This supports a genotype-phenotype correlation across molecular, cellular and clinical phenotypes.

citation: Review 2017 - Somatic SETBP1 mutations in myeloid neoplasms (PMID: 28447248)

citation: 2024 - SETBP1 activation upon MDM4-enhanced ubiquitination of NR3C1 triggers dissemination of colorectal cancer cells (PMID: 38796806)
summary: NR3C1 (glucocorticoid receptor) represses SETBP1 transcription by binding its promoter. MDM4 ubiquitinates NR3C1 and drives its proteasomal degradation, which derepresses SETBP1. SETBP1 knockdown reduced migration, invasion and EMT of CRC cells, and reduced metastasis in mouse xenografts.

citation: 2025 - Machine Learning-Based Predictive Modeling Maximizes the Efficacy of mTOR/p53 Co-Targeting Therapy Against AML (PMID: 40785506)

citation: Nuclear ubiquitination permits Hippo-YAP signal for liver development and tumorigenesis (PMID: 40379800)

citation: UBR5 mediates colorectal cancer chemoresistance by attenuating ferroptosis via Lys 11 ubiquitin-dependent stabilization of Smad3-SLC7A11 signaling (PMID: 39260061)

citation: Dragich et al. 2019 - Pathogenic WDFY3 variants cause neurodevelopmental disorders and opposing effects on brain size (PMID: 31327001)
summary: Proliferating cortical neural progenitors in human embryonic brain highly express WDFY3. Wdfy3-haploinsufficient mice show Wnt-pathway dysregulation, macrocephaly, and deficits in motor coordination and associative learning. Heterozygous mostly de novo variants (9 truncating, 4 missense) in 13 individuals cause neurodevelopmental delay. A PH-domain missense variant was associated with microcephaly.

citation: Orosco et al. 2014 - Loss of Wdfy3 in mice alters cerebral cortical neurogenesis reflecting aspects of the autism pathology (PMID: 25198012)
summary: Loss of Wdfy3 in mice causes a regionally enlarged cerebral cortex and migration defects of cortical projection neurons. Wdfy3 regulates neural progenitor divisions and neural migration in the developing brain.

citation: WDFY3 mutation alters laminar position and morphology of cortical neurons (PMID: 35733184)
summary: MADM mosaic analysis in Wdfy3 mutant mice shows a cell-autonomous requirement of WDFY3 for laminar positioning of cortical projection neurons. WDFY3 loss also alters dendritic arborization and synaptic density and morphology.

citation: Drosophila WDFY3/Bchs overexpression impairs neural function (PMID: 40000652)
summary: Overexpressing the Drosophila WDFY3 ortholog Bchs in glia or neurons impaired autophagy and locomotion. Glial overexpression increased VNC size and glial nuclei number. RNA-seq found 79 overlapping differentially expressed genes, and neuronal overexpression enriched autophagy and mitochondrial gene ontology categories.

citation: WD40 repeat and FYVE domain containing 3 is essential for cardiac development (PMID: 30428088)
summary: Wdfy3 is expressed in the developing mouse heart, peaking at E12.5, and co-localizes and physically interacts with full-length Notch1. Wdfy3 loss causes congenital heart defects, reduced NICD/Hes1/Hey1, reduced proliferation with raised p21, and reduced cardiomyocyte differentiation, with no autophagy alteration detected.

citation: Wdfy3 regulates glycophagy, mitophagy, and synaptic plasticity (PMID: 34187232)
summary: Wdfy3 haploinsufficiency in mice decreases mitophagy, leaving altered mitochondria with reduced synaptic localization and decreased synaptic density. It also impairs glycogen degradation (glycophagy), causing brain glycogen deposits and cerebellar hypoplasia.

citation: Autophagy-linked FYVE containing protein WDFY3 interacts with TRAF6 and modulates RANKL-induced osteoclastogenesis (PMID: 27330028)
summary: WDFY3 interacts with TRAF6 and is expressed at the neonatal growth plate and in osteoclasts. WDFY3-deficient macrophages show TRAF6 upregulation, increased RANKL-induced NF-κB signaling, enhanced osteoclast differentiation, and greater bone loss in vivo.

citation: Macrophage WDFY3 mitigates autoimmunity by enhancing efferocytosis and suppressing T cell activation in mice (PMID: 41027899)
summary: Myeloid Wdfy3 knockout impairs macrophage efferocytosis, increases MHC-II antigen presentation and CD4+ T cell activation, and exacerbates autoimmunity. WDFY3 overexpression enhances efferocytosis and mitigates autoimmunity.

citation: A rare genetic variant confers resistance to neurodegeneration across multiple neurological disorders by augmenting selective autophagy (PMID: 40945514)
summary: A rare WDFY3 SNP was identified as a modifier delaying Huntington's disease onset by up to 23 years. The orthologous SNP in mice is neuroprotective in two HD models and increases Alfy protein expression. Alfy overexpression also protects against phospho-α-synuclein and AT8-positive tau toxicity.

citation: ASHG 2023 - Opioid Overdose Death and Gene Dysregulation: A Transcriptome-wide Association Study in Nucleus Accumbens
summary: WDFY3 was differentially expressed with opioid overdose death in human nucleus accumbens. It was one of only 3 genes (with CITED2 and ARL4D) that also overlapped significant genes in the prefrontal cortex meta-analysis.

variant_detail: Not specified in the abstract. De novo deleterious (LoF or predicted damaging missense) variant in MOV10, listed among 12 de novo variants in candidate ASD genes.
phenotype: Autism spectrum disorder
diagnostic_reason: De novo, deleterious (LoF or predicted damaging missense) variant in a candidate ASD gene identified by WGS
center_country: Sidra Medicine (pediatric tertiary academic center), Qatar

citation: Genomic architecture of autism spectrum disorder in Qatar: The BARAKA-Qatar Study (PMID: 37805537)
variant_detail: De novo predicted LoF variant in MOV10 (specific change not given in the available text). pLI > 0.99.
phenotype: Autism spectrum disorder
diagnostic_reason: De novo predicted LoF variant in a novel candidate ASD gene with pLI > 0.99. Recurrent hits in the MSSNG and SSC cohorts were reported for most candidate genes.
