variant_detail: Three SNVs located in the CH and helicase domains of MOV10 (specific changes not given). The paper reports 13 SNVs across MOV10, PPP2R1A, PPP2CA, DCP1A and DCP2 in 41 ASD patients.
phenotype: Autism spectrum disorder
diagnostic_reason: Predicted damaging in silico, located in functional protein domains. Variant type is inferred, as the text does not state it.

citation: Mov10 suppresses retroelements and regulates neuronal development and function in the developing brain (PMID: 28662698)
phenotype: Homozygous loss of Mov10 caused early embryonic lethality (no knockout mice obtained); Mov10 heterozygotes showed reduced dendritic arborization in cultured hippocampal neurons; Reduced Mov10 in brain caused anxiety-like behavior; Reduced Mov10 caused increased activity in a novel environment; Mov10 knockout Neuro2A cells had shortened neurites; Mov10 bound retroelement RNAs and cytoskeletal mRNAs in brain

citation: RNA helicase Mov10 is essential for gastrulation and central nervous system development (PMID: 29266590)
phenotype: Maternal Mov10 knockdown (translation-blocking morpholino) caused gastrulation defects; Defective notochord and paraxial mesoderm development; Failure to neurulate; Upregulation of many mRNAs (cytoskeleton, adhesion, ECM) at stage 10.5; Delayed degradation of the miR-427 target cyclin A1; Zygotic Mov10 knockdown caused abnormal head, eye and brain development

citation: RNA helicase MOV10 suppresses fear memory and dendritic arborization and regulates microtubule dynamics in hippocampal neurons (PMID: 39915816)
phenotype: Brain-specific Mov10 deletion greatly reduced MOV10 in cortex and hippocampus; Enhanced fear memory; Elongated distal dendrites in cultured hippocampal neurons; Decreased Numa1 mRNA in hippocampus; Phenotypes rescued by NUMA1 restoration or HAUS knockdown

citation: Reduced MOV10 reveals novel functional cortical connections in an increased fear response (PMID: 42239320)
phenotype: Brain-specific Mov10 deletion mice had a thickened cortex; Abnormal dendritic arborization; Enhanced fear learning and memory; Impaired structural connectivity of canonical fear circuits on DTI; Increased cortical fMRI activity during fear memory retrieval; Increased GABRA2 expression in hippocampus

citation: Targeting age-related LINE-1 activation alleviates cardiac aging (PMID: 41571992)
phenotype: Cardiomyocyte-specific Mov10 knockout failed to suppress LINE-1; LINE-1 derepression; Cardiac dysfunction; Premature cardiac aging by 3 months of age; cGAS-STING activation; Mov10-knockout H9C2 rat cardiomyocyte cells showed senescence, attenuated by 3TC or H-151

citation: Multiple and Consecutive Genome Editing Using i-GONAD and Breeding Enrichment Facilitates the Production of Genetically Modified Mice (PMID: 37174743)
phenotype: Exon 12-14 deletion of Mov10 disrupted helicase Motif I and removed Motifs II and III; Loss of helicase activity was not essential for embryo and brain development
knockout_type: other (exon 12-14 deletion, partial loss of helicase motifs)

citation: Targeting age-related LINE-1 activation alleviates cardiac aging (PMID: 41571992)
summary: Cardiomyocyte-specific Mov10-knockout mice failed to suppress LINE-1. They developed LINE-1 derepression, cGAS-STING activation, cardiac dysfunction and premature cardiac aging by 3 months. Inhibiting LINE-1 reverse transcription (3TC) or STING (H-151) rescued senescence in Mov10-KO H9C2 cells and improved cardiac function in aged mice.

citation: MOV10 Helicase Interacts with Coronavirus Nucleocapsid Protein and Has Antiviral Activity (PMID: 34517762)
summary: MOV10 relocalizes to cytoplasmic structures with the MERS-CoV nucleocapsid (N) protein and co-immunoprecipitates with N. This interaction is conserved across human CoVs, including SARS-CoV-2. MOV10 silencing increased virus titer and N accumulation, while overexpression lowered titers about 10-fold. The antiviral effect required helicase activity (tested in CRISPR MOV10-KO cells) and was seen only with highly pathogenic CoVs. Viral RNAs were found in MOV10 complexes, suggesting RNA sequestration.

citation: MOV10 Provides Antiviral Activity against RNA Viruses by Enhancing RIG-I-MAVS-Independent IFN Induction (PMID: 27016603)
summary: MOV10 is an IFN-inducible helicase with antiviral activity against several RNA viruses that does not depend on helicase function. It enhances IRF3-mediated type I IFN induction through IKKε (not TBK1), independently of the RIG-I/MAVS pathway. Picornaviral proteases target MOV10 for degradation as an immune evasion mechanism. Shown in genome-edited knockout human cells.

citation: FMRP and MOV10 regulate Dicer1 expression and dendrite development (PMID: 34847178)
summary: Reduced MOV10 in neurons and tissues lowers DICER expression, and Dicer1 mRNA is a CLIP target of MOV10, FMRP and AGO2. The MOV10-FMRP-AGO2 complex regulates DICER1 through its 3'UTR. A DICER1 transgene rescued neurite outgrowth in Mov10-KO Neuro2A cells and branching in Mov10 heterozygote neurons.

citation: MOV10 sequesters the RNP of influenza A virus in the cytoplasm and is antagonized by viral NS1 protein (PMID: 30617221)
summary: MOV10 interacts with influenza A nucleoprotein (NP), sequesters viral RNP in the cytoplasm and promotes vRNA degradation. This depends on intact P-bodies. Viral NS1 disrupts the MOV10-NP interaction and drives lysosomal degradation of MOV10.

citation: Perturbation of the P-body component Mov10 inhibits HIV-1 infectivity (PMID: 20140200)
summary: Mov10 is a P-body-associated protein. Overexpression inhibits infectious HIV-1, other lentiviruses and MLV, acting at the pre-reverse transcription stage. siRNA knockdown modestly reduces HIV infectivity. The N-terminal half is required for activity, while helicase mutation or C-terminal truncation largely preserves it.

citation: Biological and RNA regulatory function of MOV10 in mammalian germ cells (PMID: 31088452)
summary: MOV10 is a nucleocytoplasmic protein mainly expressed in spermatogonia. Knockdown impairs spermatogonial progenitor cell proliferation and in vivo repopulation, disturbs RNA homeostasis and impairs miRNA biogenesis. MOV10 binds mRNAs with long 3'UTRs and non-coding RNAs, and nuclear MOV10 associates with splicing factors such as SRSF1.

citation: Mov10 suppresses retroelements and regulates neuronal development and function in the developing brain (PMID: 28662698)
summary: Homozygous Mov10 loss causes early embryonic lethality in mice. Mov10 is elevated in postnatal brain, where it binds retroelement RNAs and cytoskeletal mRNAs. Nuclear Mov10 suppresses retroelements by inhibiting cDNA synthesis. Heterozygotes show reduced dendritic arborization and anxiety-like behavior, and Mov10-KO Neuro2A cells have shortened neurites. Mov10, Fmrp and Ago2 bind a common set of mRNAs.

citation: Interplay between RNASEH2 and MOV10 controls LINE-1 retrotransposition (PMID: 29315404)
summary: Proteomics identified RNASEH2 as a MOV10 binding partner. The two co-localize in the nucleus, and RNASEH2 binds L1 RNA in a MOV10-dependent manner. Depleting either protein causes accumulation of L1 RNA-DNA hybrids and increased L1 retrotransposition. This loss of restriction raises expression of rheumatoid arthritis-associated cytokines and proteinases in synovial cells.

citation: ASHG 2012 - Mapping the L1 interactome reveals RISC-associated helicase MOV10 as a potent inhibitor of retrotransposition
summary: MOV10 was identified in an L1 RNP proteomic screen (IP and MS). It associates with L1 RNP alongside DDX5, DHX9, DDX17, DDX21 and DDX39A. It co-localizes with L1 ORF1p in stress granules and P-bodies. MOV10 strongly restricts L1, Alu and SVA retrotransposition in cell culture, dependent on intact helicase domains, and reduces endogenous and ectopic L1 expression. The other helicases do not strongly inhibit retrotransposition.

citation: Pbx/Meis deficiencies demonstrate multigenetic origins of congenital heart disease (PMID: 18723445)
phenotype: Pbx1 inactivation causes persistent truncus arteriosus; Reduced or absent Pbx2 or Pbx3 on a Pbx1-deficient background leads to Pbx1 haploinsufficiency; Tetralogy of Fallot-like malformations: overriding aorta with ventricular septal defect; Bicuspid aortic valves; Meis1 disruption causes cardiac outflow tract anomalies resembling Pbx mutants
knockout_type: full knockout (Pbx1 null, compound Pbx1/Pbx2/Pbx3 and Meis1 mutant alleles)

citation: Essential role for Pbx1 in corneal morphogenesis (PMID: 19797217)
phenotype: Corneal dystrophy and clouding apparent in newborns and worsening with age; Thickened corneal epithelium; Stromal infiltration by atypical basal cells; Severely disorganized stromal collagen matrix; Loss of corneal barrier function; High epithelial cell turnover with perturbed expression of developmental regulators and aberrant differentiation

citation: Loss of PBX1 function in Leydig cells causes testicular dysgenesis and male sterility (PMID: 38724675)
phenotype: Spermatogenic defects; Complete male sterility; Impaired testicular structure with disorganized seminiferous tubules; Altered fate decisions of progenitor Leydig cells; Altered transcription of steroidogenesis genes (Prlr, Nr2f2, Nedd4); Decreased testosterone; Increased pregnenolone, androstenedione and luteinizing hormone

citation: PBX1 acts as terminal selector for olfactory bulb dopaminergic neurons (PMID: 32156753)
phenotype: Loss of dopaminergic neuron identity (terminal selector function); Impaired morphological maturation of dopaminergic neurons; Derepression of alternative interneuron fates; Dysregulated alternative splicing
knockout_type: conditional knockout (Pbx1 deletion in olfactory bulb neurogenesis)

citation: PBX1 promotes development of natural killer cells by binding directly to the Nfil3 promoter (PMID: 32190943)
phenotype: Significantly reduced pre-NKP and rNKP NK-committed progenitors; Decreased Nfil3 expression in NK cells; Fewer NK precursors and NK cells, similar to Nfil3 knockout mice, with deletion of the PBX1 binding site in the Nfil3 promoter
knockout_type: conditional knockout (hematopoietic-specific Pbx1 deletion) and Nfil3 promoter PBX1-binding-site knockout

citation: Spleen hypoplasia leads to abnormal stress hematopoiesis in mice with loss of Pbx homeoproteins in splenic mesenchyme (PMID: 27075259)
phenotype: Dysmorphic, severely hypoplastic spleen in compound Pbx deficiency; Reduced numbers of HSPCs in fetal and adult spleen; Impaired hematopoietic regeneration after sublethal and lethal irradiation; Downregulation of cytokine genes including KitL/SCF and Cxcl12/SDF-1
knockout_type: conditional knockout (splenic mesenchyme-specific Pbx1 deletion, alone or with Pbx2/Pbx3 deficiency)

citation: A PBX1-IL7R axis mediates liver fibrosis in non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (PMID: 40885520)
phenotype: Significantly attenuated CDAA-HFD-induced liver fibrosis; Liver injury and steatosis not affected

citation: Zhang et al. 2020 - PBX1 promotes development of natural killer cells by binding directly to the Nfil3 promoter (PMID: 32190943)
summary: In hematopoietic-specific Pbx1 conditional knockout mice, pre-NKP and rNKP progenitors and NFIL3 expression were reduced. PBX1 binds the Nfil3 promoter directly and drives transcription, and homeodomain residue N286 controls this binding. Deleting the PBX1 binding site in the Nfil3 promoter reduced NK precursors and NK cells, as seen in Nfil3 knockout mice.

citation: Lupus susceptibility gene Pbx1 controls the development, stability, and function of regulatory T cells via Rtkn2 expression (PMID: 38536923)
summary: Pbx1 is highly expressed in human and murine Treg cells and is decreased in lupus patients and mice. Pbx1 deficiency or overexpression of the dominant-negative Pbx1-d isoform reduced Treg number, stability and suppressive function, and altered cell cycle and apoptosis genes. Pbx1 directly transactivates Rtkn2.

citation: Oligomeric self-association contributes to E2A-PBX1-mediated oncogenesis (PMID: 30894657)
summary: The E2A-PBX1 fusion oncoprotein from t(1;19) leukemia self-associates into higher-order oligomers through the PBX1 PBC-B domain, and this facilitates DNA binding and is required for transformation. Mutants that cannot self-associate are transformation-defective, but are rescued by the FKBP oligomerization domain. HOX-interaction domains of PBX1 are dispensable.

citation: Pre-B-cell leukemia transcription factor 1 contributes to liver fibrosis by enabling IL-7 signaling in HSC (PMID: 40080840)
summary: PBX1 is the most strongly upregulated transcription factor during hepatic stellate cell activation, and Notch3 drives its transcription. PBX1 knockdown reduced HSC-myofibroblast transition in vitro and liver fibrosis in mice. PBX1 activates IL7R, and IL-7/IL7R signaling interacts with TGF-β receptors to promote fibrogenesis. PBX1 correlates with IL7R and HSC activation in cirrhosis patients.

citation: PBX1 and MEIS1 up-regulate SOX3 gene expression by direct interaction with a consensus binding site within the basal promoter region (PMID: 19799567)
summary: In NT2/D1 cells, PBX1 and MEIS1 bind a conserved PBX/MEIS site in the SOX3 promoter. PBX1 is in the complex in uninduced cells, and both PBX1 and MEIS1 are in the complex after retinoic acid induction. Mutating the sites reduced RA responsiveness, and overexpression of PBX1 and MEIS1 increased endogenous SOX3 protein.

citation: Spindle function and Wnt pathway inhibition by PBX1 to suppress tumor progression via downregulating DCDC2 in colorectal cancer (PMID: 36739270)
summary: PBX1 is downregulated in colorectal cancer. Overexpressing it suppresses tumor growth and metastasis in vitro and in vivo. It acts as a transcription factor that represses DCDC2, which impairs spindle function and inhibits Wnt signaling. DCDC2 overexpression rescued the phenotypes.

citation: Expression of Pbx1b during mammalian organogenesis (PMID: 11118899)
summary: Pbx1b protein is broadly expressed throughout mouse post-implantation development, peaking in early to mid-gestation. It is initially found in condensing mesoderm and later at sites of mesenchymal-epithelial interaction in lung, kidney, tooth buds and vibrissae follicles. Its domains partially overlap with regions of proliferation.

citation: ASHG 2017 - De novo, deleterious sequence variants that alter the transcriptional activity of the homeoprotein PBX1 are associated with intellectual disability and pleiotropic developmental defects
summary: Seven patients carried de novo heterozygous PBX1 missense or truncating variants. They had a syndrome of intellectual disability, ear anomalies, heart defects, diaphragmatic hernia with lung hypoplasia, renal hypoplasia and cryptorchidism, resembling Pbx mutant mice. Functional tests of five variants showed impaired transactivation, altered nuclear translocation and abnormal interactions with TALE/HOX cofactors.

citation: ASHG 2013 - Interrogating the PBX-WNT-TP63 pathway in human nonsyndromic cleft lip/palate
sample_size: 513 white non-Hispanic families and 316 Hispanic families
summary: Family-based association testing found PBX1 rs1044263 associated with nonsyndromic cleft lip/palate in Hispanic multiplex families. PBX2 and WNT3 were also associated, and TP63 and WNT3A showed gene-gene interaction. This supports a role for the Pbx-Wnt-p63 module in human craniofacial development.

citation: Polymorphism in the PBX1 gene is related to cystinuria in Brazilian families (PMID: 30450686)
summary: The homozygous polymorphic genotype of PBX1 SNP rs17383719 was more frequent in cystinuria patients and conferred about a 3-fold increased risk. PBX1 was overexpressed 3.3-fold in patients overall, but underexpressed in those with the polymorphic homozygous genotype.

citation: Ey/Schmeisser et al. 2012 - Autistic-like behaviours and hyperactivity in mice lacking ProSAP1/Shank2 (PMID: 22699619)

citation: Rescue of behavioral and electrophysiological phenotypes in a Pitt-Hopkins syndrome mouse model by genetic restoration of Tcf4 expression (PMID: 35535852)

citation: Intrinsic properties of Tcf1 and Tcf4 splice variants determine cell-type-specific Wnt/β-catenin target gene expression (PMID: 22859735)

citation: UHRF2 promotes intestinal tumorigenesis through stabilization of TCF4 mediated Wnt/β-catenin signaling (PMID: 32372448)
summary: Uhrf2 directly interacts with and SUMOylates Tcf4, which stabilizes it and sustains oncogenic Wnt/β-catenin signaling in intestinal tumors. Uhrf2 loss in ApcMin mice inhibited tumorigenesis.

citation: The TCF4/β-catenin pathway and chromatin structure cooperate to regulate D-glucuronyl C5-epimerase expression in breast cancer (PMID: 22805760)
summary: GLCE is a target of the TCF4/β-catenin complex in breast cancer cells. TSA or 5-aza-dC/TSA treatment increased the interaction of TCF4/β-catenin with the GLCE promoter, and GLCE expression correlated with TCF4 and β-catenin in cells and primary tumors. Ectopic TCF4/β-catenin alone was insufficient, so chromatin structure also matters.

citation: TCF4 promotes erythroid development (PMID: 30315825)

citation: Nora et al. 2017 - Targeted Degradation of CTCF Decouples Local Insulation of Chromosome Domains from Genomic Compartmentalization (PMID: 28525758)
summary: Auxin-inducible degron depletion of CTCF in mouse ES cells showed that CTCF is required, in a dose-dependent manner, for CTCF-site looping and TAD insulation, including in non-dividing cells. A/B compartments stayed segregated after depletion. CTCF acts as an enhancer blocker but not as a direct barrier to heterochromatin spreading.

citation: G-quadruplexes associated with R-loops promote CTCF binding (PMID: 37552993)
summary: R-loops and G-quadruplexes co-localize with CTCF in mouse ES cells and promote CTCF binding to its motif in vitro. R-loop attenuation reduces CTCF binding in vivo, deleting a G4 motif reduces CTCF binding and alters gene expression, and G4 stabilization increases CTCF binding and alters chromatin organization.

citation: CTCF directly binds G-quadruplex structures to regulate genome topology and gene expression (PMID: 42201978)
summary: A proteomics screen identified CTCF as one of the strongest G4 binders, and biochemical work identified a CTCF mutant that prefers G4s over its consensus dsDNA motif. In mESCs reconstituted with this mutant, G4-linked loops were stronger, persistent, and less sensitive to CTCF depletion.

citation: Flavahan et al. 2016 - Insulator dysfunction and oncogene activation in IDH mutant gliomas (PMID: 26700815)
summary: IDH mutant gliomas show hypermethylation at CTCF/cohesin sites, which reduces methylation-sensitive CTCF binding. This causes loss of domain insulation and lets an enhancer contact PDGFRA. CRISPR disruption of the CTCF motif in IDH wild-type gliomaspheres upregulates PDGFRA and increases proliferation, while demethylating treatment partly restores insulation.

citation: T cell-intrinsic cGAS-CTCF regulation maintains regulatory T cell development and function (PMID: 40966077)
summary: Nuclear cGAS in Treg cells recruits CTCF to the Tnfrsf9 (4-1BB) and Tnfrsf4 (OX40) loci through chromatin interactions, sustaining their expression and TCR signaling. This cGAS-CTCF axis acts independently of STING, and Treg-specific cGAS deletion impairs tumor growth in mice.

citation: CTCF-Mediated and Pax6-Associated Gene Expression in Corneal Epithelial Cell-Specific Differentiation (PMID: 27583466)
summary: CTCF expression falls and PAX6 rises during corneal epithelial differentiation. CTCF-mediated chromatin remodeling controls PAX6 interaction with RCN1 and ADAM17 (shown by 4C, ChIP-on-chip and FISH). CTCF shRNA knockdown weakened these interactions and caused earlier onset of the differentiation genes.

citation: CTCF Expression is Essential for Somatic Cell Viability and Protection Against Cancer (PMID: 30513694)
summary: CTCF knockdown or CRISPR editing in K562 cells reduced growth and colony formation and induced cell cycle arrest. In p53-shRNA Ctcf+/- MEFs, haploinsufficiency increased proliferation, supporting CTCF as a haploinsufficient tumour suppressor. Endometrial cancers with CTCF mutations show locus-specific gene dysregulation.

citation: CTCF loss induces giant lamellar bodies in Purkinje cell dendrites (PMID: 36447271)
summary: CTCF is highly expressed in mature cerebellar Purkinje cells compared with other cerebellar neurons. Conditional deletion in mouse PCs caused progressive motor dysfunction, dendritic self-avoidance defects, giant lamellar bodies, mitochondrial swelling and eventual PC loss.

citation: Acute depletion of CTCF rewires genome-wide chromatin accessibility (PMID: 34429148)
summary: Acute auxin-induced degradation of endogenous CTCF rewired chromatin accessibility. Gains in accessibility were found near CTCF sites at promoters and insulators and were associated with increased transcription of nearby genes. A multi-omics pipeline identified 40 candidate CTCF co-regulatory partners.

citation: RNA-binding proteins mediate the maturation of chromatin topology during differentiation (PMID: 40921733)

citation: Li et al. 2015 - Integrative Analysis of Human Protein Complexes Reveals Biochemical Activities and Convergent Mechanisms of Action in Autism Spectrum Disorders (ASHG 2015)
summary: Mass spectrometry in neuronal culture purified and identified proteins co-complexed with DYRK1A, alongside ANK2, CHD8, CUL3 and POGZ. The interactors form an ASD-relevant network that is preferentially expressed in early fetal brain and regulated by FMRP and MeCP2.

citation: Walter et al. 2021 - Global kinome profiling reveals DYRK1A as critical activator of the human mitochondrial import machinery (PMID: 34257281)
summary: DYRK1A phosphorylates the mitochondrial import receptor TOM70 at Ser91, which promotes TOM70 interaction with the TOM core translocase and activates carrier protein import. DYRK1A inhibition impairs mitochondrial structure and function and triggers a protective transcriptional response.

citation: Downregulated Wnt/β-catenin signalling in the Down syndrome hippocampus (PMID: 31086297)
summary: Wnt/β-catenin signalling is downregulated in the hippocampus of adults with DS and Alzheimer's disease and in the Tc1 mouse. DYRK1A regulates Wnt bimodally: it is a negative regulator under basal conditions and enhances signalling after pathway activation.

citation: Modulation of the Wnt pathway through inhibition of CLK2 and DYRK1A by lorecivivint (PMID: 31132406)
summary: Lorecivivint inhibits DYRK1A-mediated phosphorylation of SIRT1 and FOXO1. DYRK1A siRNA knockdown in hMSCs and BEAS-2B cells modulated Wnt targets and enhanced mature chondrocyte function. Knockdown alone was sufficient for anti-inflammatory effects (NF-κB/STAT3 reduction).

citation: Embryonic organizer formation disorder leads to multiorgan dysplasia in Down syndrome (PMID: 36535930)
summary: Overexpressing human DYRK1A in zebrafish impaired the embryonic organizer and body axis, giving DS-like nervous, heart, visceral and blood abnormalities. Phosphoproteomics showed anomalous phosphorylation of β-catenin and Hsp90ab1, enhancing Wnt and inhibiting TGF-β signalling. Rebalancing Wnt/TGF-β rescued abnormal proliferation of DS HSCs.

citation: Increased dosage of DYRK1A leads to congenital heart defects in a mouse model of Down syndrome (PMID: 38266108)
summary: Genetic mapping in Dp1Tyb mice showed that a third copy of Dyrk1a causes congenital heart defects. Reducing Dyrk1a from three copies to two restored cardiomyocyte proliferation and mitochondrial respiration and rescued septation defects. Fetal DS hearts and Dp1Tyb embryonic hearts both showed reduced expression of mitochondrial respiration and proliferation genes.

citation: DYRK1A enhances antitumor immunity in type 1 conventional dendritic cells via mTORC1 activation (PMID: 42024470)
summary: DYRK1A responds to TLR and growth factor stimulation and phosphorylates TSC2 at Ser540, causing TSC2 degradation and activating mTORC1 in cDC1s. Dyrk1a ablation in cDC1s impaired antitumor immunity, and Tsc2 deletion rescued it.

citation: An inhibitory circuit-based enhancer of DYRK1A function reverses Dyrk1a-associated impairment in social recognition (PMID: 37797581)
summary: In heterozygous Dyrk1a mice, DYRK1A supports mossy fiber–PV interneuron feedforward inhibition of CA3/CA2 for social recognition. The cytoskeletal protein ABLIM3 was identified as a synaptic substrate. Ablim3 downregulation or chemogenetic PV IN activation rescued social recognition.

citation: DYRK1A is a multifunctional host factor that regulates coronavirus replication in a kinase-independent manner (PMID: 38099687)
summary: A CRISPR screen and knockout showed DYRK1A, but not DYRK1B, is required for TGEV replication through a kinase-independent, nuclear-dependent mechanism. DYRK1A loss reduced expression of the receptor ANPEP, inhibited viral entry and impaired double-membrane vesicle formation. It is also proviral for MHV, PDCoV and PSV.

citation: Impaired macroglial development and axonal conductivity contributes to the neuropathology of DYRK1A-related intellectual disability syndrome (PMID: 36402907)
summary: Dyrk1a+/- mice show increased cortical astrogliogenesis and delayed oligodendrocyte lineage progression. They also have fewer, thinner myelinated callosal axons with abnormal nodes of Ranvier and slower action potential conduction.

citation: Kang et al. 2019/2020 - Epilepsy and neurobehavioral abnormalities in mice with a dominant-negative KCNB1 pathogenic variant (PMID: 33132203)
summary: Kcnb1 G379R knock-in mice (CRISPR/Cas9) showed hyperactivity, repetitive behaviors, spontaneous and induced seizures, increased proconvulsant sensitivity, and abnormal interictal EEG. Brain immunohistochemistry showed genotype-dependent changes in Kv2.1, Kv2.2 and AMIGO-1 expression. In HEK293T cells, G379R failed to induce ER-plasma membrane junctions and reduced WT-induced junctions, consistent with a dominant-negative effect.

citation: De novo KCNB1 mutations in infantile epilepsy inhibit repetitive neuronal firing (PMID: 26477325)
summary: Kv2.1 encodes the major delayed rectifier current in pyramidal neurons. Exome data from 437 infantile epilepsy patients identified de novo R306C and G401R variants. R306C disrupted voltage-sensor sensitivity and cooperativity, while G401R abolished endogenous Kv2 currents in transfected pyramidal neurons (dominant-negative). Both mutants inhibited repetitive neuronal firing.

citation: Molecular mechanisms underlying the apoptotic effect of KCNB1 K+ channel oxidation (PMID: 23275378)
summary: Oxidized KCNB1 forms Cys73-dependent disulfide oligomers that accumulate in the plasma membrane because of defective dynamin 2-dependent endocytosis. KCNB1 localizes to lipid rafts, and the oligomers disrupt raft integrity and trigger apoptosis via c-Src/JNK signaling. The oxidation-resistant C73A variant is cytoprotective.

citation: Toxic role of K+ channel oxidation in mammalian brain (PMID: 22442077)
summary: KCNB1 is abundant in cortex and hippocampus, and its oxidant-induced oligomers are ~10-fold more abundant in old than young mouse brain and are increased in 3xTg-AD mice. The C73A variant protected neuronal cells from Aβ1-42-induced apoptosis. In C. elegans, the homolog C113S-KVS-1 protected neurons from apoptosis induced by ectopic human Aβ1-42.

citation: Stress-induced translation of KCNB1 contributes to the enhanced synaptic transmission of the lateral habenula (PMID: 38193032)
summary: Phosphorylated ribosome capture showed KCNB1 translation/expression increased in lateral habenula neurons after acute stress. shRNA knockdown of Kcnb1 altered basal firing patterns and prevented stress-induced enhancement of synaptic strength. It did not rescue despair-like behavior.

citation: Cdyl Deficiency Brakes Neuronal Excitability and Nociception through Promoting Kcnb1 Transcription in Peripheral Sensory Neurons (PMID: 35119221)
summary: The epigenetic factor CDYL deposits H3K27me3 at the Kcnb1 intron and silences Kcnb1 transcription in sensory neurons. CDYL loss increases Kv2.1 current density in DRG and reduces excitability and nociception. Kv2.1 knockdown reverses the pain-related phenotypes of Cdyl-deficient mice.

citation: Role of KCNB1 in the prognosis of gliomas and autophagy modulation (PMID: 28144039)
summary: KCNB1 expression was associated with favorable overall and progression-free survival in glioma datasets (CGGA, GSE16011, REMBRANDT). KCNB1 induced autophagy through the ERK pathway, increased apoptosis, and reduced proliferation and invasion of glioma cells. In vivo it inhibited tumor growth and increased survival.

citation: kcnb1 loss of function in zebrafish causes neurodevelopmental and epileptic disorders associated with γ-aminobutyric acid dysregulation (PMID: 40332468)
summary: In larval zebrafish, kcnb1 is expressed in neurons, oligodendrocytes and microglia across the CNS. kcnb1+/- and kcnb1-/- CRISPR knockouts showed impaired swimming, epilepsy-like activity, PTZ hypersensitivity, increased bdnf and c-Fos, and GABA dysregulation. Human Kv2.1 WT DNA restored the phenotypes.

citation: Induction of stable ER-plasma-membrane junctions by Kv2.1 potassium channels (PMID: 25908859)
summary: Clustered, non-conducting Kv2.1 induces stable ER-plasma membrane junctions in HEK293 cells and cultured hippocampal neurons, shown by TIRF and electron microscopy. The clusters act as membrane-trafficking hubs and Ca2+ signaling scaffolds. Glutamate exposure disperses the clusters and retracts the cortical ER.

citation: A KCNB1 gain of function variant causes developmental delay and speech apraxia but not seizures (PMID: 36618935)
summary: The de novo P17T variant in the Kv2.1 N-terminus increased current, shifted steady-state inactivation rightward, and reduced sensitivity to guanxitoxin-1E in whole-cell patch-clamp recordings. This gain of function is associated with developmental delay but no seizures.

citation: Wang et al. 2020 - De novo CACNA1D Ca(2+) channelopathies: clinical phenotypes and molecular mechanism (PMID: 32583268)
summary: CACNA1D encodes the pore-forming α1 subunit of Cav1.3 L-type Ca2+ channels. Somatic de novo missense variants in aldosterone-producing adenomas and germline variants in neurodevelopmental disorders cause gating changes that enhance Ca2+ influx (gain of function). The review summarizes 12 individuals with 9 high-risk pathogenic variants and discusses L-type channel blockers as a possible therapy.

citation: Ca(v)1.3 (CACNA1D) L-type Ca(2+) channel dysfunction in CNS disorders (PMID: 26842699)
summary: Cav1.3 is needed for cardiac pacemaking, hearing and hormone secretion, and is expressed postsynaptically in neurons, where it shapes firing and plasticity. Loss of function in knockout mice and humans does not cause neuropsychiatric disease. Gain-of-function de novo missense mutations are linked to ASD, seizures and primary aldosteronism, and acute pharmacological activation of Cav1.3 causes depressive-like behaviour in mice.

citation: Biophysical classification of a CACNA1D de novo mutation as a high-risk mutation for a severe neurodevelopmental disorder (PMID: 31921405)
sample_size: Two affected twins (S652L); heterologous expression in tsA-201 cells
summary: In tsA-201 cells, patch-clamp showed that S652L shifted activation and inactivation by about 13-17 mV to more negative voltages, increased window currents, slowed tail currents and increased Ca2+ levels, all gain-of-function changes. It also increased sensitivity to isradipine 3-4-fold. The S652W variant found in healthy individuals shifted gating to more positive voltages, consistent with loss of function.

citation: CaV1.3 enhanced store operated calcium promotes resistance to androgen deprivation in prostate cancer (PMID: 35193095)
summary: CACNA1D expression and a shortened 170 kDa CaV1.3 isoform increased after androgen deprivation (bicalutamide) in patients, LNCaP xenografts and cell lines. This isoform did not mediate depolarisation-induced Ca2+ influx. Instead it raised basal cytosolic Ca2+ and store-operated calcium entry (SOCE), which promoted proliferation and survival of castration-resistant cells.

citation: Data pertaining to aberrant intracellular calcium handling during androgen deprivation therapy in prostate cancer (PMID: 35496494)
summary: Among the calcium channels tested, only CACNA1D mRNA rose during androgen deprivation in the LNCaP, LNCaP-ADT, LNCaP-ABL and PC3 models. CACNA1D siRNA knockdown reduced SOCE and proliferation in PC3 cells without changing ORAI1 or STIM1 expression. Nifedipine had no effect on store release, SOCE or proliferation.

citation: Retrocochlear function of the peripheral deafness gene Cacna1d (PMID: 22678062)
summary: Conditional deletion of Cacna1d (Cav1.3) in the auditory brainstem with Egr2::Cre left the inner ear intact. The superior olivary complex lost 43-47% of its volume and 46-56% of its cells. Auditory brainstem responses were altered and Kv1.2 expression was reduced, showing a perinatal role for Cav1.3 in central auditory development.

summary: Dpf2 loss in macrophages reduced H3K27ac and H3K4me1 at the Cacna1d enhancer, lowering Cacna1d mRNA and intracellular calcium. This attenuated MAPK signaling and drove anti-inflammatory macrophage polarization. DPF2, CACNA1D and intestinal inflammation correlated positively in IBD single-cell data, organoids and clinical samples.

citation: Dominant role of CACNA1D exon mutations for blood pressure regulation (PMID: 35142739)
summary: CRISPR-Cas9 knock-in Sprague-Dawley rats carrying CACNA1D p.D307G developed elevated systolic blood pressure, higher circulating ET-1, and vascular, cardiac and renal remodeling. VSMCs showed increased Cav1.3 protein and calcineurin activity, and vascular ring tension was increased. Isradipine and the ET-1 inhibitor BQ-123 lowered blood pressure in double-mutant rats.

citation: Cellular and Genetic Causes of Idiopathic Hyperaldosteronism (PMID: 30354720)
summary: Sequencing of 99 aldosterone-producing cell clusters (APCCs) from 15 idiopathic hyperaldosteronism adrenals found somatic CACNA1D mutations in 57 (58%), compared with KCNJ5 in only 1 (1%). CACNA1D is therefore the dominant aldosterone-driver gene in these lesions and a potential therapeutic target.
